The strict figure is the downstream anchor because it nets only cash and equivalents. The $2,946.5m all-marketable-securities broad result is a sensitivity, not a substitute for the strict figure.

CIQ reconciliation: the deterministic sidecar's present reads are total debt of $9,339.0m and net debt of $4,722.7m. Both reconcile to a different vendor basis: $9,339.0m = $7,562.8m convertible-note carrying value + $1,776.2m operating-lease liabilities; $4,722.7m = $9,339.0m − $4,616.3m cash plus all marketable securities. That is a lease-inclusive, investment-inclusive broad figure, so it cannot be called strict net debt. [Capital IQ Financials → Balance Sheet, LTM/period-end Jun-30-2026 — vendor basis; ciq_facts.json, `total_debt_m` and `net_debt_m`, present]

## 5. Leverage Ratios

The reported-accounts EBITDA base is $1,184.1m LTM, calculated as FY25 GAAP-derived EBITDA of $1,275.6m less H1 FY25 $655.5m plus H1 FY26 $564.1m. It is GAAP income from operations plus depreciation and amortization, not Akamai's company-defined adjusted EBITDA. The frozen primary documents do not provide a matching LTM company-defined adjusted-EBITDA series, so no adjusted-EBITDA leverage ratio is calculated. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income, pp.54–56; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Income, p.5; Q2 2026 Supplemental Financial Information, Supplemental Metrics sheet]

| Ratio | On Reported EBITDA | On Adjusted EBITDA | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Gross debt / EBITDA | 6.39x = $7,562.8m / $1,184.1m | Not assessable — no matching LTM adjusted EBITDA disclosed | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.3–5; FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.54–56; calculation from stated rows] |
| Net debt / EBITDA — strict, canonical | 5.14x = $6,082.6m / $1,184.1m | Not assessable — no matching LTM adjusted EBITDA disclosed | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.3–5; FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.54–56; calculation from stated rows] |
| Net debt / EBITDA — broad, cash plus current marketable securities | 3.55x = $4,207.4m / $1,184.1m | Not assessable — no matching LTM adjusted EBITDA disclosed | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.3–5; FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.54–56; calculation from stated rows] |
| Net debt / EBITDA — broad, cash plus all marketable securities | 2.49x = $2,946.5m / $1,184.1m | Not assessable — no matching LTM adjusted EBITDA disclosed | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.3–5; FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.54–56; calculation from stated rows] |
| Debt / capital | 61.4% = $7,562.8m / ($7,562.8m debt + $4,748.5m common equity) | n/a | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, pp.3–4; calculation from stated rows] |
| Debt / equity | 1.59x = $7,562.8m / $4,748.5m | n/a | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, pp.3–4; calculation from stated rows] |

No normalised/mid-cycle leverage ratio is shown. A cyclical classification and a normalised EBITDA base were not provided to this specialist; no such value is inferred from the available data.

The sidecar's vendor net-debt/EBITDA read is 4.37x, using its $4,722.7m lease-inclusive, all-marketable-securities net debt and $1,079.9m CIQ EBITDA. It differs from the 5.14x strict, GAAP-derived figure for both debt/cash basis and EBITDA definition; it is reconciled here, not substituted. [ciq_facts.json, `net_debt_m`, `ltm_ebitda_m`, and `net_debt_ebitda_x`, present]

## 6. Leverage Trend

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | Latest: Q2 FY2026 | Direction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Net debt (strict §15 basis) | $3,048.8m* | $3,028.1m | $3,175.1m | $6,082.6m | Rising sharply at latest period |
| Net debt / GAAP-derived EBITDA | 2.52x* | 2.56x | 2.49x | 5.14x | Rising sharply at latest period |

\* FY2023 is a CIQ vendor-basis strict calculation whose debt composition is unconfirmed against a filing debt note; FY2024 onward uses the filed convertible-debt carrying values less filed cash. [Capital IQ Financials workbook, Balance Sheet, FY2023 column — vendor basis, data frozen 2026-09-14; FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.53; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, pp.3–4]

Strict net debt was broadly flat at roughly $3.0bn–$3.2bn through FY25, then rose $2,907.4m in H1 FY26. The arithmetic is $3,457.5m more convertible debt carrying value, partly offset by a $550.0m increase in cash: $6,082.6m − $3,175.1m = $2,907.5m. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.53; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, pp.3–4]

The direct driver was the May 2026 $3,500.0m principal issuance of 2030 and 2032 convertibles for accelerated cloud-infrastructure capital expenditure and general corporate purposes. H1 FY26 also included $615.7m of share repurchases, while $2,268.1m was used to buy marketable securities; those securities lower only the labelled broad views, not the strict measure. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), p.17; Statements of Cash Flows, pp.7–8]

## 6A. HoldCo / OpCo & Structural Subordination (if applicable)

The filing does not present a separate holding-company borrower or material holding-company debt. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–18] | Not applicable — no material HoldCo-level debt is indicated, so structural subordination cannot be sized from the data pool. |
| Upstreaming constraints (dividend blockers, regulatory) | Not disclosed in the data pool; no disclosed HoldCo debt depends on upstream dividends. | Not applicable on the available evidence. |
| Material restricted / trapped cash | $1.5m restricted cash is excluded; trapped or offshore cash is not disclosed. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Cash Flows, p.8] | The strict net-debt figure already excludes the restricted balance. |

## 7. Leverage Anchor Summary (canonical numbers for downstream agents)

- **Gross debt:** **$7,562.8m carrying value**, built as $1,705.6m current convertible notes + $5,857.3m non-current convertible notes; contractual principal is $7,640.0m. Operating-lease liabilities of $1,776.2m are excluded from this canonical debt figure. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, pp.3–4; Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–19]
- **Canonical net debt:** **$6,082.6m, strict §15 basis** = $7,562.8m gross debt − $1,480.3m cash and equivalents. This is the one downstream agents should use unless they explicitly need a broad sensitivity.
- **Broad sensitivities, not the canonical anchor:** $4,207.4m after current marketable securities, or $2,946.5m after all $3,136.0m marketable securities. Each is a labelled broad basis.
- **Cash and liquid investments:** $1,480.3m cash and equivalents; $1,875.1m current marketable securities; $1,260.9m non-current marketable securities; $1.5m restricted cash excluded. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Statements of Cash Flows, p.8]
- **EBITDA base:** **$1,184.1m LTM GAAP-derived EBITDA** (latest period, not normalised) — income from operations plus depreciation and amortization. A matching LTM company-defined adjusted-EBITDA figure is not disclosed in the frozen primary evidence.
- **Net debt / EBITDA:** **5.14x**, strict-basis net debt / LTM GAAP-derived EBITDA. Adjusted-EBITDA leverage is **Not assessable** on a matching LTM disclosed basis.
- **Reporting currency:** USD.

CIQ's present sidecar read remains useful as a separate vendor cross-check: $9,339.0m total debt, $4,722.7m net debt and 4.37x net debt/EBITDA. It is lease-inclusive and nets all marketable securities; downstream agents must retain that basis label rather than relabel it as strict net debt. [ciq_facts.json, `total_debt_m`, `net_debt_m`, `ltm_ebitda_m`, and `net_debt_ebitda_x`, present]

# Maturity Wall & Refinancing — AKAM

All amounts are USD millions under U.S. GAAP. Debt balances are at 30 June 2026; the maturity buckets and weighted-average maturity (WAM) are measured from 14 September 2026. The debt total is contractual principal of $7,640.0m, which is the maturity basis and reconciles to the $7,562.8m carrying-value gross-debt figure in `01`; the $77.2m difference is unamortized issuance costs. Operating leases are excluded because `01` treats them separately from interest-bearing debt. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20; `01_capital-structure-and-leverage.md`, Debt Stack]

## 1. Maturity Schedule

| Period | Amount Due | % of Total Debt | Instrument(s) | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Within 12 months | $1,150.0 | 15.1% | 0.375% 2027 convertible senior notes, due 1 Sep 2027 | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–19] |
| Year 2 | $0.0 | 0.0% | No contractual maturity | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–19] |
| Year 3 | $1,265.0 | 16.6% | 1.125% 2029 convertible senior notes, due 15 Feb 2029 | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–19] |
| Year 4 | $1,750.0 | 22.9% | 0.000% 2030 convertible senior notes, due 15 May 2030 | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–19] |
| Year 5 | $0.0 | 0.0% | No contractual maturity | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–19] |
| Thereafter | $3,475.0 | 45.5% | 0.000% 2032 notes ($1,750.0m) and 0.250% 2033 notes ($1,725.0m) | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–19] |
| **Total** | **$7,640.0** | **100.0%** | **Five senior unsecured convertible-note series** | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20] |

The $1,725.0m 2033 Notes are **not** a contractual near-term maturity and are therefore not added to the table. They were classified current at 30 June because holders could convert during Q3 2026 after the market-price condition was met; the company would pay the principal in cash on conversion. No holder had submitted notes for conversion through the 7 August filing date. The post-filing conversion status is not proven from the frozen evidence. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–18]

The deterministic CIQ sidecar reports the older 31 December 2025 capital-structure block: $4,105m of dated notes, $5,675m total principal including leases, 0 floating and a roughly 4.5-year WAM. That vendor block predates the $3,500m May 2026 issuance, so the primary Q2 filing's five-note schedule is used for the current wall rather than silently applying the stale vendor schedule. [ciq_facts.json, `debt_maturity_wall`, present; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), p.17]

## 2. Maturity Profile Metrics

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Weighted-average maturity (years) | 4.19 years |
| % due within 12 months | 15.1% ($1,150.0m scheduled) |
| % due within 24 months | 15.1% ($1,150.0m scheduled) |
| % due within 36 months | 31.6% ($2,415.0m scheduled) |
| Largest single maturity year (and amount) | 2030 and 2032 tie: $1,750.0m each (22.9% each) |

WAM is contractual-maturity based: ($1,150.0m × 0.96 years + $1,265.0m × 2.42 + $1,750.0m × 3.67 + $1,750.0m × 5.67 + $1,725.0m × 6.67) ÷ $7,640.0m = 4.19 years. The 12/24/36-month shares are measured from 14 September 2026; they exclude the separately stated $1,725.0m conversion contingency because it is not a maturity. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–19; calculation from stated rows]

## 3. Rate Exposure

| Metric | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Fixed-rate share | 100.0% of $7,640.0m principal | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20] |
| Floating-rate share | 0.0% drawn; the $1.0bn committed 2022 revolver and $150.0m uncommitted 2025 facility would float if drawn | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.19–20; Form 10-Q, Market Risk, p.43] |
| Weighted-average coupon | 0.30% = (($1,150.0m × 0.375%) + ($1,265.0m × 1.125%) + ($1,725.0m × 0.250%)) ÷ $7,640.0m | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), p.17; calculation from stated rows] |
| Current market refi rate (matching tenor) | 4.78% 5-year U.S. Treasury par yield on 11 Sep 2026 — a risk-free benchmark, not an all-in Akamai credit rate | [Web: U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve, 2026-09-11 (indicative, unverified)] |
| Estimated refi cost step-up (bps) | At least +448 bps: 4.78% − 0.30%, before an Akamai credit spread | [Web: U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve, 2026-09-11 (indicative, unverified); Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), p.17; calculation from stated rows] |

The +448 bps is a lower-bound comparison, not an estimate of an all-in unsecured refinancing coupon: no current Akamai credit spread or bond yield is in the frozen pool. It also does not predict the cost of another convertible. Akamai issued $3,500.0m of zero-coupon 2030 and 2032 convertibles in May 2026, whose economic price includes an equity conversion option and related hedge/warrant transactions rather than a plain-vanilla cash coupon. With no floating debt drawn, a rate move does not directly reprice the existing notes; it raises future revolver and refinancing cost instead. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20; Statements of Cash Flows, pp.7–8]

## 4. Refinancing Exposure

### Refi Funding Plan (no speculation)

| Source of repayment for next-24m maturities | Amount | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Cash on hand | $1,480.3m cash and equivalents; $1.5m separate restricted cash is excluded | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Statements of Cash Flows, p.8] |
| Current marketable securities | $1,875.1m; cash plus these current securities is $3,355.4m on a labelled broad-liquidity basis | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; calculation from stated rows] |
| Forecast FCF (or recent run-rate, labeled) | $629.9m LTM operating FCF run-rate, not a forecast: $1,447.2m CFO − $817.3m total capex | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Statements of Cash Flows, pp.55–56; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Cash Flows, pp.7–8; calculation from stated rows] |
| Revolver availability (only if availability known) | $1,000.0m committed 2022 facility with no borrowings; the filing does not separately state availability after any letters of credit or reserves, so it is not required for the market-closure conclusion | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.19–20; Capital IQ Financials → Capital Structure Summary, 2026-08-07 filing column — vendor basis, “Undrawn Revolving Credit” $1,000.0m] |
| Asset-sale proceeds (only if announced / authorized) | Unknown; none announced or authorized in the frozen evidence | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt); Item 2, Liquidity and Capital Resources] |
| New debt issuance (only if committed / announced) | No issuance announced for the 2027 maturity. Historical activity only: $3,500.0m of 2030/2032 convertibles issued in May 2026. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), p.17; Statements of Cash Flows, pp.7–8] |

The scheduled next-12-month maturity is $1,150.0m, covered by the $1,480.3m strict cash balance without relying on FCF, current marketable securities, or the revolver. The larger near-term issue is contingent: if all $1,725.0m of currently convertible 2033 Notes demanded cash principal while the $1,150.0m 2027 Notes also came due, the combined $2,875.0m would exceed cash alone but is below cash plus current marketable securities of $3,355.4m; this uses the filing's current-securities classification and is an inference, not a disclosed repayment plan. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–18; calculation from stated rows]

No current issuer rating, outlook, or rating-agency action is disclosed in the frozen pool, so rating posture is **not proven from available data**. Recent market access is proven only by the May 2026 $3,500.0m zero-coupon convertible issuance; it is evidence of then-current access, not a commitment to refinance the 2027 Notes. The conclusion is **self-funded / low refi risk** for scheduled maturities through September 2028, while the conversion contingency and continued cloud-capex cash use remain the key qualifications. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20; Item 1A, Risk Factors, pp.60–61]

## 5. Refinancing Read

The contractual wall begins with $1,150.0m (15.1% of principal) due 1 September 2027; 31.6% is due by September 2029, while $3,475.0m (45.5%) is not due until 2032–33. Cash-coupon cost is only 0.30%, but a plain unsecured refinancing at the 11 September 2026 5-year Treasury benchmark would step up by at least 448 bps before credit spread; this is a lower bound, and a convertible refinancing is not comparable to a straight bond. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20; Web: U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve, 2026-09-11 (indicative, unverified)]

The single biggest refinancing risk is the $1,725.0m 2033 series' active Q3 2026 conversion right, which is a cash-principal contingency rather than a 2033 maturity. AKAM survives the next 12 months under a market-closure assumption (no new unsecured issuance): $1,480.3m cash exceeds the $1,150.0m scheduled maturity; if the conversion contingency is added, the $2,875.0m combined amount remains below $3,355.4m of cash plus current marketable securities. This conclusion assumes those current marketable securities remain saleable at their reported value and excludes the undrawn revolver and future FCF. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20; calculation from stated rows]

# Liquidity Runway — AKAM

All figures are USD millions under U.S. GAAP, measured at 30 June 2026 unless stated otherwise. The runway is assessed from 14 September 2026 using the next-12-month maturity schedule. Free cash flow (FCF) means cash from operations (CFO) less total capital expenditure.

## 1. Liquidity Sources (committed only)

| Source | Amount | Usable? | Notes | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Cash & equivalents | $1,480.3 | Y | $1.5m of restricted cash is separately reported and excluded. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Statements of Cash Flows, p.8] |
| Liquid short-term investments | $1,875.1 | Y | Current marketable securities; no restriction is disclosed in the data pool. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Note 2 (Investments and Fair Value Measurements), pp.13–15] |
| Revolver / facilities (commitment) | $1,000.0 | Not additive | The 2022 credit agreement is a committed facility due 22 November 2028. It is shown as an availability row below, not counted twice. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.19–20] |
| Revolver availability | $1,000.0 | Y | The 10-Q reports no outstanding 2022-facility borrowings and the source-bound Capital IQ workbook reports $1,000.0m of undrawn revolving credit at 30 June 2026. The facility is not described as borrowing-base-based; Akamai was in covenant compliance at the reporting date. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.19–20; Capital IQ Financials → Capital Structure Summary, 30 Jun. 2026 filing column — vendor basis, “Undrawn Revolving Credit”] |
| 2025 uncommitted revolving credit agreement | $150.0 | N | Excluded: it is cancellable at any time and any borrowing can be due on demand. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), p.19] |
| Non-current marketable securities | $1,260.9 | N | Excluded from the near-term headline because these securities are classified non-current, even though they are marketable. | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Note 2, pp.13–15] |
| **Total usable liquidity** | **$4,355.4** |  | **$1,480.3m cash + $1,875.1m current marketable securities + $1,000.0m committed undrawn revolver.** | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.3, 19–20; Capital IQ Financials → Capital Structure Summary, 30 Jun. 2026 filing column — vendor basis] |

The $4,355.4m total contains $3,355.4m already held as cash and current securities (77.0%) and $1,000.0m of committed facility capacity (23.0%). It excludes both $1.5m restricted cash and the uncommitted $150.0m line. The current and non-current marketable-security balance is $3,136.0m, but the $1,260.9m non-current portion is deliberately not used in the near-term headline. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Statements of Cash Flows, p.8]

## 2. Near-Term Uses (next 12 months)

| Use | Amount | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Debt maturities (from 02) | $1,150.0 | 0.375% 2027 convertible senior notes due 1 September 2027. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–19; `02_maturity-wall-and-refinancing.md`, Maturity Schedule] |
| Cash interest | $23.9 LTM | $23.293m FY2025 cash interest less $11.380m H1 FY2025 plus $11.994m H1 FY2026. This is already inside CFO and therefore FCF. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Statements of Cash Flows, pp.55–56; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Cash Flows, p.8; calculation from stated rows] |
| Maintenance capex | Not disclosed separately | The company does not split maintenance from growth capex. LTM total capex is $817.3m = $819.5m FY2025 − $419.8m H1 FY2025 + $417.6m H1 FY2026; it is already inside the FCF calculation. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Statements of Cash Flows, pp.55–56; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Cash Flows, p.7; calculation from stated rows] |
| Committed dividends / buybacks | $0.0 disclosed commitment | Akamai says it does not intend cash dividends in the foreseeable future and expects no repurchases for the remainder of 2026. The $564.8m remaining authorization through June 2027 is discretionary, not a committed 12-month use. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2 (Liquidity and Capital Resources), pp.40–41; Risk Factors, p.61] |
| **Total near-term uses** | **At least $1,173.9** | **$1,150.0m maturity + $23.9m cash interest; maintenance capex is not separately disclosed. On the net-of-FCF runway basis, cash interest and total capex are not added again because FCF already includes both.** |

The $1,725.0m 2033 convertible notes are a separate liquidity contingency, not a scheduled maturity: holders could require cash principal during Q3 FY2026 after the market-price trigger was met. No holder had submitted a conversion through the 7 August filing date; post-filing conversion status is not proven from the frozen evidence. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–18]

## 3. Runway

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Total committed liquidity | $4,355.4m |
| Annual FCF (LTM) | $629.9m = $1,447.2m CFO − $817.3m total capex |
| Basis used (net-of-FCF / gross-obligations) | Net-of-FCF — FCF is positive and cash-backed, though working-capital use increased in H1 FY2026. |
| Annual net cash burn | $520.1m = ($1,150.0m scheduled maturity + $0.0m committed dividends/buybacks) − $629.9m FCF |
| Monthly net cash burn | $43.3m = $520.1m ÷ 12 |
| **Liquidity runway (months) = liquidity ÷ monthly net cash burn** | **100.5 months = $4,355.4m ÷ $43.3m** |

Formula: **$4,355.4m ÷ [(($1,150.0m + $0.0m) − $629.9m) ÷ 12] = 100.5 months.** This is a net-of-FCF calculation: the $23.9m of cash interest and $817.3m of total capex are within CFO/FCF and are not re-added. Dividing liquidity by the $520.1m annual burn would give 8.37x annual coverage, which is the same 100.5 months only after multiplying by 12.

The deterministic CIQ facts sidecar reports LTM CFO of $1,447.2m, matching the primary-source LTM calculation above. Its $710.1m levered-FCF figure is not substituted: the sidecar identifies it as a different after-interest vendor metric, while this report uses the required CFO minus total-capex FCF definition of $629.9m. [CIQ Financials → Cash Flow “Cash from Ops.”, LTM 12 months Jun-30-2026 — vendor basis; ciq_facts.json, `ltm_ocf_m`, present; CIQ Financials → Cash Flow “Levered Free Cash Flow”, LTM 12 months Jun-30-2026 — vendor basis; ciq_facts.json, `levered_fcf_m`, present]

### Seasonality / Peak Liquidity Need (Hard Check)

Working-capital seasonality is not assessable from the frozen record: only six actual quarters are available, not three full fiscal years. H1 FY2026 did use $198.3m in operating working capital versus $132.7m in H1 FY2025, but the filing does not identify this as the annual peak or disclose a peak-quarter cash need. **Peak working-capital need not disclosed — runway may be overstated.** [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Cash Flows, p.7; `01_historical-financials.md`, Quarterly Seasonality Table; `06_earnings-quality.md`, Cash Conversion Assessment]

## 4. Sources & Uses Bridge

For the scheduled 12-month maturity, $3,355.4m of cash and current marketable securities already held exceeds the $1,150.0m use by $2,205.4m; no refinancing, asset sale, FCF, or revolver draw is needed to meet that scheduled obligation. The $629.9m LTM FCF run-rate covers 54.8% of the maturity, leaving $520.1m (45.2%) to be funded from liquidity in the runway calculation; the $1.0bn revolver is not required in this base case. The 100.5-month figure nevertheless depends on FCF continuing while accelerated cloud-infrastructure spending is funded: the May 2026 note issuance was intended in part for accelerated capital expenditure. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20; Item 2 (Liquidity and Capital Resources), p.41; calculation from stated rows]

## 5. Liquidity Read

The base liquidity runway is **100.5 months** on the clean net-of-FCF basis, with $4,355.4m of committed liquidity and a $520.1m annual financing shortfall after LTM FCF. The base case does not require external refinancing for the $1,150.0m September 2027 scheduled maturity; even excluding the $1.0bn revolver, cash plus current marketable securities cover it 2.92x. The single biggest liquidity risk is a full $1,725.0m cash-principal conversion of the currently convertible 2033 Notes during Q3 FY2026: combined with the scheduled $1,150.0m maturity, $2,875.0m would leave only $480.4m of cash plus current marketable securities before operating cash needs, although it remains within the $4,355.4m committed-liquidity total. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20; calculation from stated rows]

## balance-sheet-survival / 04_coverage-and-covenants.md

_Source: `balance-sheet-survival/04_coverage-and-covenants.md`_

# Coverage & Covenants — AKAM

All figures are USD millions and use U.S. GAAP. Ratios use the latest twelve months (LTM) through 30 June 2026 unless a different basis is stated. EBITDA is **GAAP-derived**, calculated as income from operations plus depreciation and amortization; it is not Akamai's company-defined Adjusted EBITDA. Interest is **gross income-statement interest expense**, not netted against the company's interest and marketable-securities income.

## 1. Coverage Ratios

| Ratio | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| EBITDA / interest | 35.73x = $1,184.094m / $33.143m | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income and Cash Flows, pp.54–56; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Income and Cash Flows, pp.5, 7–8; calculation from stated rows] |
| EBIT / interest | 13.75x = $455.678m / $33.143m | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income, p.54; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Income, p.5; calculation from stated rows] |
| (EBITDA − capex) / interest | 11.07x = ($1,184.094m − $817.311m) / $33.143m | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, pp.55–56; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Cash Flows, pp.7–8; calculation from stated rows] |
| Fixed-charge coverage | 0.23x = ($1,184.094m − $817.311m) / ($33.143m interest + $1,149.992m scheduled convertible-note repayment + $398.715m operating-lease cash payments) | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, pp.55–56; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Cash Flows, pp.7–8; calculation from stated rows] |

The LTM EBITDA build is FY2025 $1,275.555m less H1 FY2025 $655.527m plus H1 FY2026 $564.066m. LTM interest is $30.759m less $14.951m plus $17.335m; the latest half-year interest includes coupon interest, debt-issuance-cost amortization, credit-facility interest and commitment fees, less capitalized interest. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income, p.54; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Interest Expense), p.20]

Fixed-charge coverage is a strict historical LTM measure: it includes the $1,149.992m May 2025 convertible-note repayment that fell in the period, rather than treating that debt repayment as if it were an operating expense. The next stated final maturity is the $1,150.0m 2027 Notes on 1 September 2027; the 2033 Notes were classified current at 30 June 2026 because a conversion condition was met, but no holder had submitted notes for conversion through the filing date. Excluding the past bullet repayment gives a **0.85x reference**, but it is not an LTM fixed-charge ratio because it removes one historic LTM charge; it is shown only to separate the past refinancing event from recurring capex, interest and lease cash demands. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20]

Calculation audit — executed Bash command using the filing inputs above:

```bash
awk 'BEGIN {ebitda=1275.555-(306.044+349.483)+(194.778+369.288); interest=30.759-14.951+17.335; capex=819.500-419.789+417.600; lease=329.674-156.036+225.077; repayment=1149.992; cash_surplus=ebitda-capex; ltm_fixed=interest+repayment+lease; printf "LTM EBITDA less capex=%.3f; LTM fixed charges incl. scheduled 2025-note repayment=%.3f; LTM fixed-charge coverage=%.2fx\n", cash_surplus, ltm_fixed, cash_surplus/ltm_fixed; printf "Reference excluding that past bullet repayment (not an LTM fixed-charge ratio)=%.2fx\n", cash_surplus/(interest+lease)}'
```

```text
LTM EBITDA less capex=366.783; LTM fixed charges incl. scheduled 2025-note repayment=1581.850; LTM fixed-charge coverage=0.23x
Reference excluding that past bullet repayment (not an LTM fixed-charge ratio)=0.85x
```

Cash quality is a qualifier, not an adjustment to the table. FY2025 CFO was $1,518.8m against GAAP-derived EBITDA of $1,275.6m (119.1%), so the EBITDA base is cash-backed on that measure. But CFO benefits from adding back $459.4m of stock-based compensation, and the earnings-quality review identifies recurring stock-based compensation and restructuring exclusions; coverage should therefore not be recast onto management's adjusted earnings. [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.54–56; Q2 2026 Supplemental Financial Information, GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliation sheet]

The deterministic CIQ sidecar's authoritative workbook read is 32.6x LTM interest coverage, using $1,079.9m CIQ EBITDA. The filing-based result is 35.73x because its GAAP-derived EBITDA is $1,184.1m, $104.2m (8.8%) higher; the vendor read implies LTM interest of $33.126m — **inference from the vendor read, not from filings** — which is consistent after rounding with the filed $33.143m. This is a disclosed EBITDA-definition difference, not a replacement of the filing-based coverage ratio. [CIQ Financials→Income Statement, EBITDA ÷ Interest Expense, LTM Jun-30-2026 — vendor basis; ciq_facts.json, `interest_coverage_x` and `ltm_ebitda_m`, present]

## 2. Covenant Inventory

| Covenant | Threshold | Current Actual | Headroom | Source |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Maximum consolidated leverage ratio (ceiling) | Not disclosed | Not disclosed; company states it was compliant at 30 Jun 2026 | Not assessable | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |
| Minimum interest coverage | Not disclosed in the data pool | Not disclosed | Not assessable | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |
| Minimum liquidity / net worth | Not disclosed in the data pool | Not disclosed | Not assessable | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |
| Springing covenant trigger (e.g., revolver utilization threshold) | Not disclosed | $0.0m drawn under the $1,000.0m committed 2022 facility | Not assessable | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |
| Equity cure rights (Y/N, limits) | Not disclosed | Not assessable | Not assessable | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |
| Other: restrictions on subsidiary debt, liens and fundamental changes | Qualitative negative covenants; exceptions and qualifications not quantified | Company states compliance | Quantitative headroom not assessable | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), p.20] |

The $1,000.0m 2022 Credit Agreement expires on 22 November 2028, has no drawing at the reporting date, and contains the disclosed maximum consolidated leverage-ratio covenant. The separate $150.0m 2025 facility is uncommitted, cancellable at any time and callable on demand; it is not evidence of a covenant cushion or usable committed liquidity. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20]

### Covenant EBITDA Definition & Quality (required if headroom is computed)

No numerical covenant headroom is computed because the filing does not disclose the maximum ratio, the actual ratio, or the agreement's EBITDA definition.

| Item | Value / Description | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Covenant EBITDA definition summary | Not disclosed in the data pool | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |
| Addbacks permitted (types) | Not disclosed in the data pool | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |
| Addback caps / limits | Not disclosed in the data pool | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |
| Is covenant EBITDA materially above reported EBITDA? | Not assessable | [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |

Headroom quality is unknown: a compliance statement cannot establish whether the lender's EBITDA includes material addbacks or whether those addbacks have caps. The synthesis layer should retain covenant headroom as **Not assessable** and apply the module cap for missing covenant-EBITDA/addback detail; the executed 2022 Credit Agreement and amendments are the single document needed to remove this limitation.

## 3. Headroom & Breach Proximity

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Tightest covenant | Not assessable — the only disclosed financial test is a maximum consolidated leverage ratio, without its threshold or current actual |
| Headroom on tightest covenant (%) | Not assessable |
| EBITDA decline that would breach it (approx.) | Not assessable — the ceiling and Covenant EBITDA definition are absent |
| Debt increase that would breach it (approx.) | Not assessable — the ceiling and current covenant leverage are absent |

For a maximum-leverage covenant, the direction-correct formula would be `(threshold − actual) / threshold`; a positive result would be remaining headroom. Neither input is disclosed, so naming a breach percentage, EBITDA decline or debt increase would be invented. The filing confirms compliance only and does not establish whether the covenant is springing, the relevant debt netting, or equity-cure capacity. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20]

## 4. Coverage / Covenant Read

LTM GAAP-derived EBITDA covers gross interest expense by 35.73x and EBIT covers it by 13.75x; after total capex, the interest-only coverage is 11.07x. The strict LTM fixed-charge result is 0.23x because it includes the $1.150bn scheduled 2025 Note repayment and $398.7m operating-lease cash payments, so it describes the cash burden of a refinancing year rather than evidence that coupon interest cannot be paid. The only disclosed financial covenant is a maximum consolidated leverage ratio: Akamai reported compliance, but without the threshold, current ratio or Covenant EBITDA definition, the tightest covenant, its headroom and the operational move that would breach it are Not assessable.

## 5. Contingency Read

The largest known gross obligation is $2,331.0m of lease-related payments and uncommenced commitments at 31 December 2025, 46.8% of same-date equity; it is live, although $1,570.0m was already recognized as lease liabilities and management expects $731.2m of future sublease income to offset part of the gross payments. Purchase commitments, litigation claims, tax-audit claims and performance bonds are not quantified, while indemnities are contractually unlimited; undisclosed exposures cannot be ruled out, and the balance-sheet synthesis should apply its module cap where the leverage condition is met. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 12, pp.79–80; Note 13, pp.80–81]

## balance-sheet-survival / 06_downside-stress-test.md

_Source: `balance-sheet-survival/06_downside-stress-test.md`_

# Downside Stress Test — AKAM

All figures are USD millions under U.S. GAAP unless stated otherwise. EBITDA is GAAP-derived operating profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization; it is not Akamai's company-defined Adjusted EBITDA. The base uses LTM EBITDA of $1,184.1m and LTM FCF of $629.9m, both cash-backed in the limited sense that LTM CFO was $1,447.2m. That cash conversion still contains recurring stock-based compensation and a rising working-capital outflow, so adjusted EBITDA is not substituted. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income and Cash Flows, pp.54–56; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Income and Cash Flows, pp.5, 7–8]

## 1. Base Case (today)

The 30 June balance sheet predates the July 2026 LayerX acquisition. The filing says Akamai paid approximately $205.0m cash, subject to post-closing adjustments, but does not disclose LayerX's cash, debt, interest expense or EBITDA. I therefore use a **known-component pro forma**: reported strict net debt plus the $205.0m cash consideration, no target EBITDA contribution, and usable liquidity less the same cash outflow. This is not a complete acquisition pro forma; the actual numerator and denominator could each move when target financial information is available. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 6 (Acquisition)]

Management said the deal should have no material full-year FY26 revenue impact and should reduce non-GAAP EPS by about $0.12 across Q3–Q4. That does not quantify EBITDA, target net debt or target cash, but it gives no basis to add EBITDA to the survival denominator. [Q2 FY2026 earnings call, CFO prepared remarks]

The CIQ sidecar confirms LTM CFO of $1,447.2m, matching the filing build. It reports $9,339.0m total debt, $4,722.7m net debt and $1,079.9m EBITDA, rather than this report's $7,562.8m debt carrying value, $6,082.6m reported strict net debt and $1,184.1m GAAP-derived EBITDA. The vendor debt includes $1,776.2m operating leases and its net-debt figure also nets cash plus marketable securities; its EBITDA definition is different. Those are material basis differences, so the filing-based strict series remains the stress anchor. [CIQ Financials → Cash Flow, “Cash from Ops.”, LTM Jun-30-2026; CIQ Financials → Balance Sheet, “Total Debt” and “Net Debt”, Jun-30-2026 — vendor basis; CIQ Financials → Income Statement, “EBITDA”, LTM Jun-30-2026 — vendor basis; `ciq_facts.json`, `ltm_ocf_m`, `total_debt_m`, `net_debt_m`, and `ltm_ebitda_m`, present]

The business is in an investment transition, not identified as a deep commodity or cyclically calibrated name in the cross-module work; no extra historical-trough haircut is added. Costs related to data-centre capacity and customer IT spending are material, but a historic EBITDA peak-to-trough range is not established in the available record. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Item 2, pp.30–34; Business-model External Dependency, §§1–3]

## 2. Stress Scenarios

All cases assume the September 2027 $1,150.0m maturity is paid from existing liquidity: no new unsecured refinancing for 12 months. They use the known-component LayerX pro forma above. For the working-capital case, the $198.3m is an incremental cash outflow; it reduces both FCF and cash, so strict net debt rises by $198.3m in that column.

FCF scaling is a stated assumption, not a filing forecast: `FCF(h) = $629.879 − $1,184.094 × h × (1 − 25%)`, where `h` is the EBITDA haircut. The 25% is FY2025's $150.4m tax expense divided by $602.4m pretax income. It holds cash interest, total capex and lease cash payments fixed; it gives no credit for price, cost, hedge, capex or dividend mitigation. The rate case has no effect because there is no drawn floating-rate debt and no revolver draw is required. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income, p.54; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20]

| Metric | Base | −30% EBITDA | −40% EBITDA | −60% EBITDA | −40% + WC shock | −40% + rates +200bp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| EBITDA | $1,184.1 | $828.9 | $710.5 | $473.6 | $710.5 | $710.5 |
| Net debt / EBITDA | 5.31x | 7.59x | 8.85x | 13.28x | 9.13x | 8.85x |
| EBITDA / interest | 35.73x | 25.01x | 21.44x | 14.29x | 21.44x | 21.44x — not applicable; $0 drawn floating debt |
| Tightest covenant headroom | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable |
| Covenant breach? (Y/N) | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable |
| 12-month liquidity gap (uses − sources) | $(3,630.3) surplus | $(3,363.9) surplus | $(3,275.1) surplus | $(3,097.4) surplus | $(3,076.7) surplus | $(3,275.1) surplus |
| Survives without external action? | Y, on known components | Y, on known components | Y, on known components | Y, on known components | Y, on known components | Y, on known components; rate shock has $0 effect |

The liquidity-gap row is `scheduled maturity − (usable liquidity + stressed FCF)`; a negative number is a surplus. Covenant rows are not replaced with an assumed market covenant because `04` supplied no labeled threshold, covenant EBITDA definition or debt numerator. The reported compliance statement alone cannot show a breach point. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20]

All scenarios assume zero management mitigation — this is a survival bound, not a forecast; the earnings module's realised-offset case (`earnings/07` §2) is the expected-outcome read.

Calculation audit — executed Bash command using the table inputs:

```bash
awk 'BEGIN {
  E=1184.094; ND=6082.571+205.0; I=33.143; FCF=629.879;
  L=4355.4-205.0; O=1150.0; tax=0.25; WC=198.332;
  n=6; names[1]="Base"; h[1]=0; w[1]=0; names[2]="-30%"; h[2]=.30; w[2]=0;
  names[3]="-40%"; h[3]=.40; w[3]=0; names[4]="-60%"; h[4]=.60; w[4]=0;
  names[5]="-40%+WC"; h[5]=.40; w[5]=WC; names[6]="-40%+rates"; h[6]=.40; w[6]=0;
  for(i=1;i<=n;i++) { e=E*(1-h[i]); nd=ND+w[i]; fcf=FCF-E*h[i]*(1-tax)-w[i]; gap=O-(L+fcf); printf "%-10s EBITDA %.3f; ND/EBITDA %.3fx; coverage %.3fx; FCF %.3f; gap %.3f\n", names[i],e,nd/e,e/I,fcf,gap }
  printf "Liquidity h %.6f; 6x leverage h %.6f\n", (L+FCF-O)/(E*(1-tax)), 1-ND/(6*E)
}'
```

```text
Base       EBITDA 1184.094; ND/EBITDA 5.310x; coverage 35.727x; FCF 629.879; gap -3630.279
-30%       EBITDA 828.866; ND/EBITDA 7.586x; coverage 25.009x; FCF 363.458; gap -3363.858
-40%       EBITDA 710.456; ND/EBITDA 8.850x; coverage 21.436x; FCF 274.651; gap -3275.051
-60%       EBITDA 473.638; ND/EBITDA 13.275x; coverage 14.291x; FCF 97.037; gap -3097.437
-40%+WC    EBITDA 710.456; ND/EBITDA 9.129x; coverage 21.436x; FCF 76.319; gap -3076.719
-40%+rates EBITDA 710.456; ND/EBITDA 8.850x; coverage 21.436x; FCF 274.651; gap -3275.051
Liquidity h 4.087827; 6x leverage h 0.114996
```

## 3. Break Points

| Break Point | EBITDA Decline That Triggers It |
|---|---:|
| Tightest covenant breaches | **Not assessable.** The filing identifies a maximum consolidated leverage covenant but not its threshold, numerator or Covenant EBITDA. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20] |
| Committed liquidity exhausted within 12 months | **Does not exhaust on an EBITDA decline alone.** Mechanical solve is 408.8%, above a 100% EBITDA decline. |
| Net leverage exceeds 6.0x | **11.5% decline.** This is an analyst monitoring threshold for refinancing, not a disclosed covenant. |

The covenant formula for a maximum leverage test is `h = 1 − debt metric / (T × EBITDA)`. Here both `T` and the debt metric are undisclosed, so solving it would fabricate precision. The liquidity solve is `h = ($4,150.4 + $629.879 − $1,150.0) / ($1,184.094 × 75%) = 4.0878`, or 408.8%; at a 100% decline the model still has $2,742.2m surplus against the scheduled maturity. The 6.0x monitoring solve is `h = 1 − $6,287.571 / (6.0 × $1,184.094) = 11.5%`. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.3; Note 6 (Acquisition); Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20; calculation from stated rows]

The 2033 conversion right is the material unmodeled timing risk. The notes were convertible in Q3 FY26; none had been submitted by the filing date, and post-filing status is not in the frozen evidence. If all $1,725.0m of principal converted alongside the $1,150.0m scheduled maturity, the $2,875.0m use would still leave a $1,372.4m surplus in the −60% case including the committed revolver, or a $372.4m surplus using only cash plus current marketable securities. This is a calculated liquidity sensitivity, not a statement that conversion will occur. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Conversion Rights of the Notes), pp.17–18; calculation from stated rows]

## 4. Survival Read

On the known-component LayerX pro forma, AKAM survives the modeled 30–60% EBITDA decline and a 12-month closure of unsecured refinancing markets: even the −60% case has a $3.10bn scheduled-maturity liquidity surplus. The first modeled warning is refinancing leverage, not cash: strict net leverage rises above the labeled 6.0x monitoring level after an 11.5% EBITDA decline and reaches 13.28x at −60%; cash interest coverage remains 14.29x because the existing $7.64bn note principal is fixed-rate and mostly zero- or low-coupon. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 (Debt), pp.17–20; calculation audit above]

The actual covenant break point is not proven because the credit agreement's threshold and calculation rules are absent. That missing document, plus LayerX's debt, cash and EBITDA, is more valuable than a guessed covenant. The company does not need an equity raise, distressed asset sale or waiver in these cash tests, but a deeper earnings decline would leave it dependent on maintaining a very high leverage profile and on the undisclosed covenant terms rather than on a lack of cash. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 6 (Acquisition); Note 7 (Revolving Credit Facilities), pp.19–20]

Partial data: covenant threshold, covenant EBITDA definition, debt numerator, cure rights, and LayerX debt/cash/EBITDA are not disclosed in the frozen pool. Covenant headroom and its EBITDA breach point are therefore Not assessable; the acquisition stress is a known-component pro forma, not a complete target pro forma.

## competitive-intel — module synthesis

# Competitive-Intel Module — AKAM (Synthesis)

## Abstract

The frozen pool holds an independently defined three-company peer set—Cloudflare, Fortinet and Fastly—but no competitor transcript, peer results release or permitted broker call summary, so it provides no real call benchmark. The net read-through for AKAM’s Q3 2026 print is therefore Not assessable, with neither weight nor a direction-confidence band assignable. AKAM’s narrative neither survives nor fails the cross-check because every peer comparison is untestable. Reporting peers speak to 0% of AKAM’s revenue exposure in this run; Security, Delivery and other cloud applications, and CIS are all uncovered. Verdict: this module records a complete evidence gap and should not move the master synthesizer’s beat/miss view. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — AKAM, §§1–5; Narrative Triangulation — AKAM vs Peers, §5]

## 1. Verdict Block

- **Net read-through direction:** Not assessable — no eligible, already-reported peer call exists. AKAM has sourced Q3 2026 consensus and guidance bars, but a subject bar cannot substitute for peer evidence. [Peer Read-Through — AKAM, §§2, 4]
- **Read-through weight:** Not assessable — there is no read to weight. [Peer Read-Through — AKAM, §§2, 6]
- **Read-through direction confidence:** Not assessable — no directional proposition exists, so no §10 probability band or basis can be assigned. [Peer Read-Through — AKAM, §2]
- **Narrative triangulation verdict:** Not testable. [Narrative Triangulation — AKAM vs Peers, §5]
- **Peer-coverage of subject /100:** **0/100** (higher is better; not inverted). [Q2 2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers), p.23; Competitive-Intel Data Triage — AKAM, §2]
- **Benchmark data-sufficiency /100:** **0/100** (higher is better; not inverted; mandatory no-usable-call floor applied). [data/AKAM/ frozen-generation manifest, generation `c4d3e6273c464a9c80ac6b2d5376f06f8686a7fd7d1593a78ba6741c81cf1d6c`, source inventory and totals]
- **Dispersion:** Not assessable — zero peer calls produce no valid peer denominator. [Peer Dimension Matrix — AKAM, §2]
- **Single most important peer signal:** None. The frozen evidence set contains no admissible peer management statement or peer-reported result; that absence is an evidence-status finding, not a signal about AKAM. [Peer Claim Extraction — AKAM, Per-Peer Claim Blocks]
- **Biggest contradiction or corroboration of the subject’s narrative:** None testable; no peer claim exists on a matched scope and window. [Narrative Triangulation — AKAM vs Peers, §§1–3]

## 1B. Score Builds (reproducible — CLAUDE.md §12)

### Peer-coverage of subject /100 (higher is better; not inverted)

Only read-through-eligible and scope-overlapping peers count. There are none. The category weights use AKAM’s Q2 2026 revenue mix.

| AKAM exposure | Revenue weight | Covered by an eligible peer? | Covered contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Security | 55.0% | No — no peer call admitted | 0.0% |
| Delivery and other cloud applications | 36.0% | No — no peer call admitted | 0.0% |
| Cloud infrastructure services (CIS) | 9.0% | No — no peer call admitted | 0.0% |
| **Total** | **100.0%** |  | **0.0%** |

The build is `round(covered_exposure_pct) = round(0.0%) = 0/100`. The named peers’ product overlap adds no coverage without an admitted call. [Q2 2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers), p.23; Business-model Competitive Map — AKAM, §2]

### Benchmark data-sufficiency /100 (higher is better; not inverted)

| Component | Build | Points |
|---|---|---:|
| Reporting-peer breadth | `N = 0` eligible distinct peer companies; no partial peers | 0/40 |
| Exposure coverage | `round(0.0% × 0.30) = 0` | 0/30 |
| Source quality | No eligible verbatim transcript and no broker paraphrase | 0/20 |
| Peer-set provenance | Peer set inherited from `business-model/08_competitive-map.md` | 10/10 |
| **Mechanical subtotal** | **0 + 0 + 0 + 10** | **10/100** |

Because the pool holds no usable call at all—neither a verbatim transcript nor a permitted broker paraphrase—the mandatory no-usable-call floor resets the whole benchmark data-sufficiency score from the 10-point mechanical subtotal to **0/100**. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — AKAM, §§1, 3–5; data/AKAM/ frozen-generation manifest, generation `c4d3e6273c464a9c80ac6b2d5376f06f8686a7fd7d1593a78ba6741c81cf1d6c`, source inventory and totals]

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation (CLAUDE.md §8)

- **Strongest bear read-through:** Not assessable. No peer management signal exists from which to infer pressure on AKAM’s next print.
- **Strongest bull read-through:** Not assessable. No peer management signal exists from which to infer support for AKAM’s next print.
- **Single killer contradiction:** None identifiable from available peer evidence; the comparison is untestable, which is not proof that no contradiction exists. [Narrative Triangulation — AKAM vs Peers, §§2, 5]
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** No peer-based disconfirming evidence is visible because no peer evidence was admitted. The absence of a peer call is not evidence in favor of AKAM’s narrative. [Peer Dimension Matrix — AKAM, §§1–3]
- **What data would change this conclusion:** No AKAM line-item boundary can be carried from `03` because `03` produced no peer-derived proposition. AKAM’s Q3 2026 revenue consensus of $1,118.153m and normalized-EPS consensus of $1.68032 are subject bars, not peer-derived falsifiers, and must not be repurposed as such. The module conclusion can change only after an admissible Cloudflare, Fortinet or Fastly call covering all or part of July–September 2026 creates a scope-matched proposition; that proposition must then specify an AKAM line item, a boundary, the Q3 2025 same-basis comparable and whether the peer covered the full window. [Capital IQ Estimates Report, Guidance worksheet, current FQ3 2026 fields — vendor export; Peer Read-Through — AKAM, §§2, 5]
- **What would force a downgrade / rejection:** The module’s current directional contribution is already withdrawn as Not assessable. Reject any future directional use if the peer evidence is not an admissible management statement or reported result, or if its calendar window and product scope do not overlap AKAM’s tested line item. [Competitive-Intel Module Rules, G1–G3 and G5]

## 2. Specialist Roll-Up

| Specialist | Verdict Line | Biggest Finding |
|---|---|---|
| competitive-intel-triage | **Insufficient.** | The frozen generation contains no usable competitor transcript or permitted broker paraphrase; 0% of AKAM’s revenue categories is covered. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — AKAM, §§2, 5] |
| peer-claim-extraction | **Insufficient — no usable competitor call in the pool.** | No management claim or reported peer figure can be extracted for Cloudflare, Fortinet or Fastly. [Peer Claim Extraction — AKAM, Per-Peer Claim Blocks] |
| peer-dimension-matrix | **Not assessable — the matrix and dispersion are empty.** | All 11 dimensions lack a matched-window, scope-tagged peer observation. [Peer Dimension Matrix — AKAM, §§1–3] |
| peer-readthrough-to-subject | **Not assessable — no already-reported peer with overlapping scope.** | AKAM’s subject bars exist, but they cannot establish a peer-based beat or miss direction. [Peer Read-Through — AKAM, §§2, 4] |
| peer-narrative-triangulation | **Not testable.** | No peer claim can corroborate or contradict AKAM’s demand, pricing, share, margin, cost or guidance narrative. [Narrative Triangulation — AKAM vs Peers, §§1–5] |

## 3. Reconciliation

No material disagreements. All five specialists treat the absence of peer calls as an evidence gap rather than as information about the peers or AKAM. The subject’s sourced consensus and guidance bars do not conflict with that result: they define what AKAM may beat or miss, but without peer evidence they do not create a competitive read-through. The only mechanical interaction is that 0% covered exposure produces a **Low** weight ceiling under the exposure rule, while zero eligible peers produces no directional read at all. The no-read state governs: final direction, weight and confidence are all **Not assessable**; Low is only the otherwise-applicable ceiling, not an assigned weight. [Peer Read-Through — AKAM, §§2, 4, 6; Competitive-Intel Data Triage — AKAM, §4]

## 4. Score Cap Application

| Cap Trigger | Applied? (Y/N) | Affected | Final Cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| No peer transcripts | Y | read-through | Not assessable — no verbatim call or permitted broker paraphrase exists |
| Only one peer | N | weight | Not triggered; `N = 0`, so the stronger no-usable-call state applies |
| No peer reported the window | Y | current read-through | Not assessable |
| Exposure uncovered (by coverage band) | Y | net weight | Low ceiling because covered exposure is 0%; superseded by the Not assessable no-read state |
| Peer set self-selected | N | net weight | Not triggered; the competitive map supplied the peer set |
| Broker-paraphrase only | N | tone | Not triggered; no permitted paraphrase exists |

The resulting exposure ceiling is **Low**, but there is no eligible read to which that ceiling can apply. Under the three-move-together rule for an unassessable net direction, the final read-through weight and direction confidence are both **Not assessable**, not Low. [Competitive-Intel Module Rules, Score Caps and Coverage of the Subject’s Exposure; Competitive-Intel Data Triage — AKAM, §4]

## 5. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- **Beat/miss and scenario input:** Net peer read-through is **Not assessable**; weight is **Not assessable**; direction confidence is **Not assessable**. There is no load-bearing peer signal. Do not move AKAM’s Q3 2026 beat/miss or scenario view from this module. The revenue and normalized-EPS consensus bars are subject data only, not peer evidence. [Peer Read-Through — AKAM, §§2, 4]
- **Falsifiers and rejection triggers:** There is no peer-derived AKAM line-item boundary to inherit as a §8 kill criterion. Do not recast $1,118.153m of Q3 revenue consensus or $1.68032 of normalized-EPS consensus as peer falsifiers. A future read requires an eligible peer call, then a named AKAM line item, boundary, Q3 2025 same-basis comparable, and full- versus sub-window label. Reject the read if period, scope or management-source tests fail. [Peer Read-Through — AKAM, §§2, 5]
- **Narrative and candor:** Narrative triangulation is **Not testable**. No peer-based contradiction, corroboration or candor conclusion should enter the master thesis; missing peer evidence is not evidence of misleading disclosure. [Narrative Triangulation — AKAM vs Peers, §§2–5]
- **Coverage gap:** Peers cannot speak to **100%** of AKAM’s Q2 2026 revenue mix in this run: Security 55.0%, Delivery and other cloud applications 36.0%, and CIS 9.0% are all uncovered. Do not turn product-list overlap into a whole-company read. [Q2 2026 Form 10-Q, Note 11 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers), p.23]
- **Binding caps:** The absence of any usable peer call and any comparable-window peer result binds the read-through at Not assessable. The 0% exposure band also imposes a Low hypothetical ceiling, but no H/M/L weight is assigned because no read exists. The peer set itself was independently inherited, so no self-selected-peer cap applies. [Competitive-Intel Data Triage — AKAM, §4]

## 6. Simple Summary

- The named peer set is real, but the frozen pool contains no usable peer calls or permitted broker summaries.
- The already-reported peers imply nothing testable for AKAM’s next print; direction, weight and confidence are all Not assessable.
- AKAM’s story did not pass or fail the peer test because there was no peer evidence to test it against.
- The benchmark is blind to 100% of the company: Security 55.0%, Delivery and other cloud applications 36.0%, and CIS 9.0%.
- This module is useful only as an evidence-gap and cap for the master synthesizer; it supplies no beat/miss signal or peer-derived kill criterion.

## management-governance — module synthesis

_Source: `management-governance/99_management-governance-synthesis.md`_

# Management-Governance Module — AKAM (Synthesis)

## Abstract

Akamai’s leaders look competent but weakly aligned. Capital deployment has not proven per-share value creation: FY2021–FY2025 cash acquisitions were $598.8m+$872.1m+$106.2m+$434.1m+$55.1m=$2.066bn, and H1 buybacks of $615.744m were 278% of $221.174m cash after total capex. [Capital IQ Financials, Cash Flow, FY2021–FY2025 — Tier-5 vendor; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, p.7] Pay disclosure is incomplete; 94.4% of available grants were service-based, founder-CEO ownership was 1.9%, and observed sales were plan-driven. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 18, pp.84–86; Web: 2026 DEF 14A, pp.26–27, filed 2026-03-31 — unverified] The largest risk is that repeated acquisitions, including another $205m for LayerX, lack disclosed deal-level returns. Free cash flow (FCF) means cash from operations (CFO) minus total capex. “Strict” net debt means total debt minus cash equivalents; net debt/EBITDA divides that figure by earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortization. Earnings per share (EPS) is profit allocated per diluted share; GAAP is the reported accounting basis, while non-GAAP removes company-selected items. Stock-based compensation (SBC) is employee pay settled in shares or share-linked awards; profit after tax (PAT) is bottom-line profit, and key management personnel (KMP) are the senior people who direct the company.

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** FY2021–FY2025 cash acquisitions were $598.8m + $872.1m + $106.2m + $434.1m + $55.1m = $2.066bn, LayerX added $205m, and the admitted evidence contains no deal-by-deal return on invested capital (ROIC—the profit earned per dollar invested), synergy-delivery, impairment, or alternative-use comparison; H1 buybacks of $615.744m were 278.4% of $221.174m strict FCF while shares outstanding fell by 1.120m, or 0.8%. [Capital IQ Financials, Cash Flow sheet, FY2021–FY2025 — Tier-5 vendor; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 6, p.17, Statements of Cash Flows, p.7, and Statements of Stockholders’ Equity, pp.9–12]
- **Strongest bull point:** Q2 2026 revenue, non-GAAP EPS, and non-GAAP margin all landed inside management’s prior ranges; H1 repurchases reduced shares outstanding by 1.120 million, and the FY2025 audit and internal-control-over-financial-reporting (ICFR) opinions were unqualified. [Q1 FY2026 earnings release, Financial Guidance, p.2; Q2 FY2026 earnings release, Results, p.1; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Stockholders’ Equity, pp.9–12; FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.51–52, 94]
- **Single killer risk:** Capital continues to move into acquisitions, cloud infrastructure, and buybacks without returns above the cost of capital, leaving minority holders with higher leverage and no proven per-share value gain.
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** H1 share count fell 0.8%, the new convertible notes have zero coupons, and CIQ reported 32.6× LTM EBITDA/interest coverage; these facts weaken an immediate financial-distress interpretation but do not establish sound capital returns. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Stockholders’ Equity, pp.9–12 and Note 7, pp.17–20; ciq_facts.json, interest_coverage_x, 2026-09-14 — Tier-5 vendor]

## 3. Reconciliation

- **Dedicated capital-allocation work supersedes the quick read.** The business-model quick read scored capital allocation at 45 and did not apply the serial-acquirer cap. The dedicated specialist examined the five-year cash-acquisition record, LayerX, buyback funding, filed convertible principal, return-on-capital trend, and missing deal returns; its 38 score and RF-CAP-004 therefore govern this synthesis. [Business-Model Capital Allocation Governance, AKAM, 2026-09-14; Capital Allocation Scorecard, AKAM, §§1–5, 2026-09-14]
- **Ownership alignment is not the same as shareholder-rights structure.** Agent 04 refused to assign a numerical ownership-alignment score because the complete transaction and pledge data are absent. Agent 05 could assess a public-proxy board and rights structure, but its raw 67 was capped at 60. This synthesis uses 60 for shareholder friendliness while preserving ownership alignment as insufficient.
- **The subsidiary count is 46, not 57.** Agent 07 initially counted 57 entries. Agent 09 re-counted the primary Exhibit 21.1 and found 46 legal entities; the primary-source count wins, with no omission inferred. [Related-Party & Group Forensics, AKAM, finding 09-019, 2026-09-14]
- **Noname identity is resolved, not cleared.** Agent 07 left Noname Gate Ltd. and “Noname Security” pending. Agent 12 matched the latter to the acquired business/trade label of Noname Gate, not a predecessor of Akamai; Israeli registry, primary court, and sanctions coverage remain incomplete, so neither row becomes resolved-clean. [Regulatory, Legal & Compliance, AKAM, §1A, 2026-09-14]
- **The legal sweep adds a sub-material case without changing the contingency conclusion.** Agent 10 had filings-only litigation coverage. Agent 12 found a secondary-source report of the $3.741 million Barkan claim, 0.079% of Q2 equity, but no primary docket; it stays Amber and does not trigger RF-CMP-001. [Regulatory, Legal & Compliance, AKAM, §§1A and 8, 2026-09-14]
- **Candor’s filing-timeliness input remains unproven.** Agent 06 used a neutral placeholder because agent 12 had not yet completed its work; agent 12 later verified only one of the required 12 quarters. The 54 candor score is retained, but no positive timeliness claim is carried.

## 5. Stewardship Summary

Management has a stable operating bench and met the one completed quarterly guide, but a single interval cannot prove a durable promises-versus-delivery record. [Management & Track Record, AKAM, §§2–5, 2026-09-14] Capital use has not yet shown per-share value creation: acquisitions lack disclosed return scorecards, buybacks exceeded strict free cash flow, GAAP diluted EPS fell from $3.52 in FY2023 to $3.07 in FY2025, and return on capital declined on the vendor series. [Capital Allocation Scorecard, AKAM, §§1–5, 2026-09-14] The available incentive evidence points more toward retention and size than per-share returns, while 1.9% founder-CEO ownership gives exposure without control and the complete ownership record is missing. [Incentives & Compensation, AKAM, §§2–4; Ownership & Insider Behavior, AKAM, §§1–5, 2026-09-14] Minority holders have an independent chair and one-share/one-vote structure, but the 41.9% stock-plan opposition, conditional single-trigger vesting, takeover limits, and adjusted-earnings emphasis weaken protection. [Board & Shareholder Rights, AKAM, §§1–5; Candor & Disclosure Quality, AKAM, §§2–5, 2026-09-14] The main reason not to entrust more capital without proof is the combination of repeated acquisitions, rising leverage, and no deal-level return record. [Capital Allocation Scorecard, AKAM, §5, 2026-09-14]

## 6. What Would Change The Stewardship Verdict?

| Current Verdict | What Would Strengthen It | What Would Weaken It | Data Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Misaligned or weak stewardship | Two to three years of deal-level returns above the cost of capital; strict FCF covering buybacks; GAAP EPS and return on capital improving; lower equity burn; a board response to the 41.9% dissent; full legal/person checks without adverse findings | Another debt-funded acquisition without a return hurdle; impairments or divestitures exposing overpayment; strict leverage staying above 5×; buybacks continuing above FCF; widening GAAP-adjusted gaps; a material undisclosed matter or adverse person finding | First: frozen FY2026 DEF 14A. Then deal scorecards, complete Form 4/13D/13G and pledge data, current Form AP and fee table, intercompany/RPT ledger, official legal/registry/sanctions results, and the next annual lease schedule |

## 7. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- Treat the stewardship verdict as **misaligned or weak**: FY2021–FY2025 cash acquisitions were $598.8m + $872.1m + $106.2m + $434.1m + $55.1m = $2.066bn, and LayerX added $205m, without disclosed deal-level returns.
- **Non-Negotiable Gate: PASS, with 116/179 checklist items answered.** No hard disqualifier, Critical flag, Disqualifying controller/KMP, or material undisclosed legal matter was confirmed.
- Capital deployment has not proven per-share value creation: H1 share count fell, but buybacks were 278.4% of strict FCF, GAAP diluted EPS fell from $3.52 to $3.07 in FY2023–FY2025, and vendor return on capital fell.
- Incentives and ownership do not prove alignment with minority holders: 94.42% of FY2025 grant units were service-based, burn was 4.73%, conditional single-trigger vesting exists, and founder-CEO ownership was 1.9%.
- **People read:** 24 Clean, coverage-limited; 0 Minor, 0 Material, 0 Disqualifying; one unnamed CSO. Aaron Ahola is the clearest named monitor because his Nasdaq council recusal controls are unverified, not because an adverse record was found. No open §24 Filter 1 integrity signal, and no person trips a gate. [People Integrity Dossiers, AKAM, §§1–2, 2026-09-14]
- **Checklist read:** 64.8% answered; nine Red items — A4-02 audit-firm calibre, A4-13 firm/partner discipline, A6-04 equity burn/overhang, A6-05 conditional single-trigger vesting, A6-09 problematic pay practice, A7a-01 lease-related commitments, A8-05 recurring restructuring, A10-03 stock-plan dissent, and A14-01 leverage. RPT & leakage risk at 45 is the binding Checklist Risk because the aggregate RPT ledger and group cash topology are missing.
- The biggest governance flag is RF-CAP-004, High: repeated acquisitions without return proof; it caps capital allocation at 50 and floors Governance risk at 60.
- Business-model/01 hard-disqualifier result, verbatim: **“No disqualifier triggered.”**
- §24 rejector filters: serial acquirer tripped, applying CapAlloc max 50 and GovRisk floor 60; turnaround, structurally unaligned owner, and unresolved-integrity filters did not trip.
- Partial-data caps apply to incentive alignment, usefulness, shareholder friendliness, board reliance, audit assurance, RPT risk, people/network integrity, legal risk, and confidence. The legal floor moved LegalRisk from 32 to 40; other capped scores were already inside their limits.
- The single highest-value next data request is the filed FY2026 DEF 14A in the frozen evidence set.
- **This module supersedes business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance. Treat this module’s governance verdict and scores as the primary governance read.**
- Preserve RF-DISC-002 in the cross-module forensic roll-up; recurring SBC/restructuring and the large GAAP-to-adjusted gap may compound with earnings-quality or balance-sheet flags.

## 8. Simple Summary

- Management met the one completed quarterly guide, but one quarter is not a long record. [Q1 FY2026 earnings release, Financial Guidance, p.2; Q2 FY2026 earnings release, Results, p.1]
- Capital has not proven per-share value creation; acquisitions lack return scorecards and buybacks exceeded strict FCF. [Capital IQ Financials, Cash Flow sheet, FY2021–FY2025 — Tier-5 vendor; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, p.7]
- The available pay evidence mainly rewards service and retention, with high burn and conditional single-trigger vesting. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 18, pp.84–86 and Exhibit 10.5, §6(c)–(e)]
- The founder-CEO owns 1.9%; observed sales were plan-driven, no observed open-market buy was found, and the full record is missing. [Web: 2026 DEF 14A, pp.26–27, filed 2026-03-31 — unverified public SEC filing supplement; Web: SEC Forms 4, 2025-11-07 to 2026-07-15 — unverified public filing sweep]
- An independent chair, 8/9 independent directors, and one-share/one-vote help minority holders, but stock-plan dissent and takeover limits weaken the read. ## 6. Sufficiency Verdict

- **Verdict:** Partial
- **Reason:** The frozen pool has current audited and interim filings, transcripts, an audit report, commitments disclosure, and three-year capital-allocation history, but it omits the proxy/compensation disclosure, full ownership and insider-transaction data, board and voting disclosure, related-party detail, and auditor-fee disclosure required for a complete governance read.
- **Specialists that can run:** management track record; capital allocation; candor; people dossiers (from the seed register, subject to the discovery loop); audit quality (except fee independence); RPT/group forensics (limited); contingent liabilities; accounting forensics; regulatory/legal (subject to its independent database sweep). Incentives, ownership, and board/shareholder-rights agents run only to record their data-limited conclusions and caps.
- **Hard disqualifier already flagged by business-model/01_disqualifier-scan?** N — no verdict lock was triggered. That scan separately preserves the ownership/pledging and RPT gaps as not assessable. [business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md, Verdict-Lock Signal]
- **Active partial-data caps:**
  - No proxy / compensation disclosure: incentive alignment maximum 50; overall usefulness maximum 70.
  - No ownership / comprehensive insider-transaction data: shareholder friendliness maximum 60.
  - Board independence, committee, election, and rights read: not assessable from the signature roster.
  - No related-party note: RPT quantification not assessable; Amber disclosure finding.
  - No auditor-fee disclosure: audit & assurance quality maximum 65; confidence maximum 80.
- **Critical missing items:**
  - FY2026 DEF 14A, including CD&A, named-executive pay, beneficial ownership, board committees/independence, related-party transactions, auditor fees, voting and shareholder-rights disclosures.
  - Form 4 / authoritative insider-transaction history and Schedule 13D/13G or equivalent ownership data.
- **Single highest-value missing document:** FY2026 DEF 14A proxy statement.

## 3. Stated Strategy & Targets

Management’s stated strategy is to use Akamai’s distributed platform to provide security, compute, delivery and AI-infrastructure services, with investment focused on higher-growth security and Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS). [FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 1, pp. 3–5; Item 7, p. 29] In Q2, management said that CIS commitments signed so far in 2026 exceeded $2.8 billion and anticipated total-company revenue growth accelerating into the low teens in 2027; this is a forward target, not delivered revenue. [Q2 2026 earnings call, CEO prepared remarks, p. 4] Its published FY2026 targets are revenue of $4.445–$4.530 billion, CIS constant-currency growth of at least 50%, Security growth in the high single digits, a mid-single-digit decline in Delivery and other cloud applications, and non-GAAP operating margin of 25%–26%. [Q2 2026 earnings call, CFO prepared remarks, pp. 7–8]

## 5. Management Read

This is a stable, founder-led management group: the CEO has served 13.7 years and the CFO 7.5 years, while the five-role operating group has a 5.5-year median role tenure. [Web: 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 24–26 — unverified, used only for background and tenure] The only completed current-year guide was kept, but Q2 reduced FY2026’s revenue and EPS high ends and extended the non-GAAP margin range down to 25%; this is a limited, mixed execution record rather than proof of a long record of promises kept. [Q1 2026 earnings release, Financial guidance, p. 2] vs [Q2 2026 earnings release, Results and Financial guidance, pp. 1–2]

The biggest management signal is that the CIS-led plan is measurable but still unproven: signed commitments above $2.8bn and a low-teens 2027 growth target do not establish revenue conversion or return on the extra capital. [Q2 2026 earnings call, CEO and CFO prepared remarks, pp. 4, 6–8]

# Capital-Allocation Scorecard — AKAM

AKAM reports in USD under U.S. GAAP. This is a FY2023–FY2025 scorecard, with H1 2026 used only to test the latest direction. FCF means cash from operations (CFO) less total cash capex, including capitalized internal-use software.

## 1. Uses of Capital (3–5 years)

| Use | Cumulative Amount | Currency | % of CFO (or FCF) | Source |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Acquisitions (cash) | 595.4 | USDm | 13.6% of $4,386.4m CFO | [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies Inc NasdaqGS AKAM Financials.xls, Cash Flow sheet, FY2023–FY2025] |
| Buybacks | 2,374.6 | USDm | 54.1% of CFO; 110.4% of $2,151.6m FCF | [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies Inc NasdaqGS AKAM Financials.xls, Cash Flow sheet, FY2023–FY2025; data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, FY2025 Form 10-K, Statements of Cash Flows, p.55] |
| Dividends | 0.0 | USDm | 0.0% of CFO | [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies Inc NasdaqGS AKAM Financials.xls, Cash Flow sheet, FY2023–FY2025] |
| Capex | 2,234.8 | USDm | 51.0% of CFO | [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, FY2025 Form 10-K, Statements of Cash Flows, p.55] |
| Debt repayment | 1,490.0 | USDm | 34.0% of CFO | [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies Inc NasdaqGS AKAM Financials.xls, Cash Flow sheet, FY2023–FY2025] |

The amounts are cash-flow categories, so they are not additive measures of CFO: debt repayment can be funded with refinancing or balance-sheet cash. The three-year FCF build is $4,386.4m CFO less $2,234.8m total capex = $2,151.6m. Buybacks therefore exceeded internally generated FCF by $223.0m before acquisitions and debt repayment. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, FY2025 Form 10-K, Statements of Cash Flows, p.55]

## 2. M&A Scorecard

|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|

FY2024 restructuring included impairments of acquired intangible assets and capitalized internal-use software, but the filing does not attribute those charges to this cash-flow line. | Cash-flow export reports no divestiture proceeds; lost alternatives are not quantified. | [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies Inc NasdaqGS AKAM Financials.xls, Cash Flow sheet, FY2024; data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, Note 10 (Restructuring), pp.74–75] |

FY2025 restructuring again included impairments of acquired technology/customer intangibles and capitalized internal-use software, without a deal-level attribution. | Not proven from available data. | [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies Inc NasdaqGS AKAM Financials.xls, Cash Flow sheet, FY2025; data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, Note 10 (Restructuring), pp.74–75] |
| LayerX (post-quarter acquisition) | 2026 | 205.0 USDm cash | The available filing identifies the acquisition but not a measurable synergy or return target. | Too early; no delivered metric in the record. | Not proven from available data. | [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., Q2 2026.pdf, Form 10-Q, Note 6 (Acquisition)] |

**Serial-acquirer + opportunity-cost test (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 4).** Cash acquisitions were $598.8m, $872.1m, $106.2m, $434.1m, and $55.1m in FY2021–FY2025: $2,066.3m in total. Three annual amounts were more than $400m, and the programme continued with the $205.0m LayerX acquisition in July 2026. This is a serial-acquirer pattern for score-cap purposes, even though the available evidence does not show debt-funded acquisitions near or above AKAM’s own value. No deal-level return, synergy delivery, or comparison with the organic cloud build is disclosed; do not infer success from the acquisition rationale. **RF-CAP-004 is triggered (High); the capital-allocation score is capped at 50, although the raw score below is already lower.** [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies Inc NasdaqGS AKAM Financials.xls, Cash Flow sheet, FY2021–FY2025; data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., Q2 2026.pdf, Form 10-Q, Note 6 (Acquisition)]

ROIC is the profit earned for each $100 invested. The CIQ return-on-capital series is not the required incremental-ROIC formula, so it is not substituted for it. Its decline nevertheless matters when total capex rose to $819.5m in FY2025 and the company recorded FY2023–FY2025 restructuring actions of $135.326m, including product retirements and impairments of capitalized software and acquired intangibles; not all of those charges are impairments or attributable to a particular deal.
