## 5. Capital-Allocation Read

**Mixed.** The best proven use is the H1 2026 buyback result: 4.998m shares repurchased exceeded 3.879m issuances/reissues and reduced shares outstanding by 1.120m, so the programme was not just dilution offset. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., Q2 2026.pdf, Form 10-Q, Statements of Stockholders’ Equity, pp.9–12]

The worst use is the repeated acquisition programme: $2.066bn of FY2021–FY2025 cash acquisitions and $205.0m for LayerX have no disclosed return, synergy, or alternative-use comparison in the admitted evidence, which triggers the serial-acquirer cap rather than an assumption of value creation. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies Inc NasdaqGS AKAM Financials.xls, Cash Flow sheet, FY2021–FY2025; data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., Q2 2026.pdf, Form 10-Q, Note 6 (Acquisition)]

The single biggest signal is the May 2026 $3.500bn convertible issuance for accelerated cloud infrastructure: filed convertible principal reached $7.640bn at June 30 while H1 strict FCF was only $221.174m and buybacks were $615.744m. The contrary fact is that the notes carry zero coupons and CIQ reports 32.6x LTM EBITDA/interest coverage, so this is not an immediate cash-interest distress call; it is a return-on-investment and balance-sheet-capacity concern. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., Q2 2026.pdf, Form 10-Q, Note 7, pp.17–20; Statements of Cash Flows, p.7; ciq_facts.json, interest_coverage_x, 2026-09-14 — CIQ vendor basis]

Per-share value creation is therefore not proven: H1 share count improved, but FY2023–FY2025 GAAP diluted EPS fell from $3.52 to $3.07 and the vendor return-on-capital series also fell. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, FY2025 Form 10-K, Statements of Operations, p.54; ciq_facts.json, multi_year_trajectory, 2026-09-14 — CIQ vendor basis]

# Incentives & Compensation — AKAM

**Partial-data limit:** The FY2026 definitive proxy, which contains the CEO/CFO compensation tables, annual-bonus and long-term-incentive (LTIP) targets and weights, pay ratio, director-pay table, and say-on-pay result, is not in the frozen evidence set. FY2025 Form 10-K incorporates that proxy by reference rather than reproducing it. Incentive alignment is therefore **not assessable at executive level** and is capped at 50/100. [FY2025 Form 10-K, cover — Documents Incorporated by Reference; Item 11—Executive Compensation, p.95]

## 1. Compensation Structure

| Executive | Base | Annual Bonus | Long-Term Incentive | Cash vs Equity Mix | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| F. Thomson Leighton, CEO | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Not disclosed for the CEO; company-wide plan includes service-, TSR- and financial-performance RSUs/restricted stock | Not assessable | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 11—Executive Compensation, p.95] |
| Edward J. McGowan, CFO | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Not disclosed for the CFO; company-wide plan includes service-, TSR- and financial-performance RSUs/restricted stock | Not assessable | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 11—Executive Compensation, p.95] |

Reporting currency is USD and the filing basis is U.S. GAAP; the latest annual period is FY2025 ended 2025-12-31. The missing proxy is material: company-wide stock-plan disclosures do not show the CEO/CFO pay mix or what each executive can earn.

## 2. Performance Metrics

| Plan | Metric | Weight | Per-Share/Returns or Size-Based? | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Annual bonus | CEO/CFO annual-bonus metrics and weights are not disclosed in the frozen pool | Not disclosed | Not assessable | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 11—Executive Compensation, p.95] |
| Company-wide FY2025 service awards | Continued service; 6.499m of 6.883m FY2025 RSU/restricted-stock/DSU grants (94.42% by units) | 94.42% of company-wide FY2025 grant units; not an executive-pay weight | Neither: retention/time-based, not a per-share value measure | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 18—Stock-Based Compensation, pp.85–86] |
| Company-wide FY2025 market-based awards | Relative total shareholder return (TSR) against a peer group; 0.249m grant units | 3.62% of company-wide FY2025 grant units; not an executive-pay weight | Returns-based | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 18—Stock-Based Compensation, pp.85–86] |
| Company-wide FY2025 performance-based awards | Defined internal financial metrics, not named in the filing; 0.135m grant units | 1.96% of company-wide FY2025 grant units; not an executive-pay weight | Not assessable: the filing does not identify whether the metrics are per-share/returns or size-based | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 18—Stock-Based Compensation, pp.85–86] |

The disclosed mix is a grant-unit mix across employees, officers, directors, consultants and advisers, not the CEO/CFO LTIP mix. It establishes that TSR and financial-performance awards exist, but cannot establish the actual executive scorecard or whether it rewards revenue, absolute EBITDA, EPS, ROIC, free cash flow per share, or something else.

## 4. Incentive Alignment Read

**Mixed.** The disclosed equity plan contains TSR and financial-performance awards, but the filing gives neither the CEO/CFO cash/equity mix nor their actual performance metrics and weights; executive pay cannot therefore be judged as per-share-value or size-led. The strongest disclosed negative is conditional single-trigger change-of-control equity vesting, alongside FY2025 award burn of 4.73% of FY2025 weighted-average basic shares—above the 3% Red band—although these grants are company-wide rather than CEO/CFO-only. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 18, pp.84–86; Exhibit 10.5, §6(c)–(e)]

# Ownership & Insider Behavior — AKAM

The frozen evidence set does not include the 2026 proxy or a Capital IQ ownership export. The FY2025 Form 10-K incorporates its ownership disclosure by reference to that proxy, while the CIQ facts sidecar marks insider activity, open-market activity, top holders and institutional-holder trend as missing. The SEC filings cited as web sources below are useful context, but are not frozen-pool evidence and are labelled unverified. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 12, p.95; CIQ facts sidecar, ownership fields, frozen 2026-09-14 — vendor data]

Thomson Leighton, co-founder and CEO | 1.9% (2,759,456 shares) | Common Stock | The source identifies 2,529,963 trust-held shares and 108,358 foundation shares; it also includes 72,000 RSUs vesting within 60 days. It does not establish the cash cost or acquisition history of the trust-held stake. | [Web: SEC EDGAR 2026 preliminary proxy, Security Ownership, pp.26–27, filed 2026-03-05 (unverified)] |

Cash-purchase history is not disclosed in the available source. | [Web: SEC EDGAR 2026 preliminary proxy, Security Ownership, pp.26–27, filed 2026-03-05 (unverified)] |

Total insider ownership is 2.3% (3,317,206 shares across 18 executive officers and directors) as of February 20, 2026. This SEC-web figure includes shares acquirable within 60 days, so it is not a current economic-interest or cash-purchase measure. [Web: SEC EDGAR 2026 preliminary proxy, Security Ownership, pp.26–27, filed 2026-03-05 (unverified)]

## 5. Ownership / Insider Read

Founder-CEO ownership is meaningful as personal exposure but not control: Leighton held 1.9% and the entire executive-officer/director group 2.3% at the disclosed February date. The trust-held founder stake is distinct from the small near-term RSU component, but its original cash cost is not proven. [Web: SEC EDGAR 2026 preliminary proxy, Security Ownership, pp.26–27, filed 2026-03-05 (unverified)]

The observed $2.15m of sales were all under Rule 10b5-1 plans, while vesting and tax-withholding entries are not discretionary buys or sales. The main minority-holder risk from this lens is evidence quality: the missing frozen proxy/ownership export means actual pledges, complete net insider activity, institutional trends and any shareholder bloc cannot be assessed; they must not be assumed benign. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 12, p.95; CIQ facts sidecar, ownership fields, frozen 2026-09-14 — vendor data]

# Board & Shareholder Rights — AKAM

## 1. Board Composition

**Verdict: Board independent; shareholder rights adequate but constrained.** The latest detailed board disclosure is the filed 2026 DEF 14A, which was not included in the frozen evidence generation. It is used below only as a clearly labelled public SEC-filing supplement; it does not remove the frozen-pool gap. The frozen FY2025 Form 10-K incorporates the proxy into Items 10–14, confirming that the missing proxy is where the board, ownership, related-party and shareholder-rights disclosures belong. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, FY2025 Form 10-K, Items 10–14, filed 2026-02-20]

At the May 13, 2026 annual meeting, shareholders elected nine directors. Eight of the nine were classified independent by the company under Nasdaq rules; the exception was co-founder and CEO F. Thomson Leighton. The Board chair, Dan Hesse, is independent and separate from the CEO. This is a favourable structural fact, not proof that every director is free of all commercial influence. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, filed 2026-03-31, pp. 10–11 and 27–28 — public filing not in frozen pool; SEC 8-K, filed 2026-05-13, Item 5.07 — public filing not in frozen pool]

| Feature | Current read | Evidence and qualification | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Board size and independence | Nine directors elected; eight classified independent (88.9%). | Board size is the post-meeting elected slate. Independence classification is the proxy’s, not an independent legal conclusion. ## 2. Tenure & Refreshment

Using the disclosed initial appointment years for the nine elected directors and calendar 2026, the median tenure is approximately seven years (calculated: 1, 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 28 years). This is below the module’s nine-year independent-director median reference point. The conclusion carries two qualifications: Leighton’s 28-year tenure is as founder/CEO rather than independent director, and the calculation is an analyst calculation from disclosed appointment years, not a company-reported statistic. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 19–26 — public filing not in frozen pool]

Four of nine 2026 nominees are women and three are racially or ethnically diverse under the proxy’s stated definitions. The Board also states that it considers diversity in nominations. This supports diversity disclosure, but not a conclusion on representation of every stakeholder group. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 12–13 — public filing not in frozen pool]

## 3. Related-Party Transactions & Group Leakage

The FY2025 Form 10-K incorporates related-party disclosure from the absent proxy, so the frozen evidence alone cannot support a complete related-party transaction (RPT) conclusion. The public 2026 DEF 14A states that no transaction requiring Item 404(a) disclosure occurred in 2025 and describes a review process for possible transactions involving directors, officers and their immediate family. This is a favourable legal-disclosure statement, not proof of zero RPTs under a broader economic definition. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 13, p. 95; SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, filed 2026-03-31, p. 39 — public filing not in frozen pool]

| Potential relationship / control | Amount / terms disclosed | Approval / disclosure read | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Item 404(a) reportable transactions in 2025 | The proxy reports none. | The proxy says transactions involving a director or the General Counsel are reviewed by disinterested Audit Committee members; other executive-officer transactions are reviewed by the General Counsel after notice to the Audit Committee and Board chairs. | Favourable but scope-limited. It does not prove the absence of all transactions with all affiliates. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, p. 39 — public filing not in frozen pool] |
| Burger / BT International commercial relationship | $36.4m sales; $1.4m purchases in 2025. | Proxy says the transactions were in the ordinary course, on normal commercial terms and each less than 1% of the applicable party’s revenue. | Independence-context relationship; do not classify as an Item 404 RPT without the filing doing so. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 28–29 — public filing not in frozen pool] |
| Ranganathan / OpenText commercial relationship | $1.3m sales; $0.5m purchases in 2025. | Same proxy qualification: ordinary course, normal commercial terms and below 1% of applicable revenue. | Independence-context relationship; do not classify as an Item 404 RPT without the filing doing so. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 28–29 — public filing not in frozen pool] |

## 4. Takeover Defenses & Voting Rights

AKAM has one disclosed Nasdaq-listed common-stock class and the proxy states one vote per common share. That supports a simple common-share voting structure. Its charter and by-laws nevertheless contain standard U.S. takeover defences: the Board can issue undesignated preferred stock, fill vacancies, impose advance-notice rules for nominations and proposals, and Delaware’s business-combination statute can restrict certain transactions with 15% holders for three years without Board approval. These provisions can make a change of control harder even if an offer could benefit shareholders. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, FY2025 Form 10-K, cover page and pp. 24–25; SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 108–110 — public filing not in frozen pool]

| Right / defense | Current position | Minority-holder implication |
|---|---|---|
| Common-share voting | One vote per common share; no unequal common-share voting class disclosed. | Positive. The conclusion is limited to common stock; the charter’s undesignated preferred-stock authority remains. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 108–110 — public filing not in frozen pool; FY2025 Form 10-K, pp. 24–25] |
| Director elections | Annual elections; majority voting in uncontested elections and a resignation policy for a director who does not receive more “for” than “against” votes. | Positive accountability mechanism. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 108–110 — public filing not in frozen pool] |
| Proxy access | A shareholder or group may nominate up to 20 nominees or 25% of the Board (whichever is greater) after holding at least 3% for three years. | Usable but demanding for a small holder. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 108–110 — public filing not in frozen pool] |
| Special meetings | Following shareholder approval at the May 2026 annual meeting, holders of at least 25% may demand a special meeting, subject to ownership and continuing-hold requirements. | A meaningful right, but the 25% threshold is high for dispersed holders. [SEC 8-K, filed 2026-05-13, Items 5.03 and 5.07 — public filing not in frozen pool] |
| Written consent | Charter / by-laws require shareholder action at a duly called meeting rather than written consent. | Restrictive. [SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, pp. 108–110 — public filing not in frozen pool] |
| Anti-takeover provisions | Advance notice, Board vacancy-filling, blank-check preferred-stock authority, and Delaware Section 203 are disclosed. | Restrictive; no inference is made about how the Board would use them in a future offer. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, pp. 24–25] |

## 4A. Shareholder Voting & Dilution

The key voting signal is the approval of an amendment to the 2013 Stock Incentive Plan that added 8.0m shares, with 66,180,915 votes for and 47,672,263 against. Excluding abstentions, the against share was **41.9%**: 47,672,263 / (66,180,915 + 47,672,263). This is far above the module’s 20% high-opposition trigger. The outcome is a shareholder-approved plan amendment, not evidence that the plan is improper; the 8-K does not state the Board’s response to the scale of opposition. [SEC 8-K, filed 2026-05-13, Item 5.07 — public filing not in frozen pool]

## 4B. Corporate-Actions Fairness

No group merger, delisting, preferential allotment, rights issue or qualified-institutional placement was identified in the FY2025 Form 10-K or Q1/Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q disclosures reviewed. This is a statement about the reviewed filings, not a claim that no corporate action can occur. The 8.0m-share stock-plan amendment is not a preferential allotment, but it is a dilution-related action and had material opposition. [data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., 2025.pdf, FY2025 Form 10-K, filed 2026-02-20; data/AKAM/Akamai Technologies, Inc., Q1 2026.pdf and Q2 2026.pdf, Forms 10-Q; SEC 8-K, filed 2026-05-13, Item 5.07 — public filing not in frozen pool]

| Action | Fairness read | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Group merger / affiliate buyout | No such action identified in the filings reviewed; no transaction fairness analysis is therefore available. | Not Applicable |
| Stock-plan share increase | 8.0m shares approved, but 41.9% of votes cast were against. Plan terms and shareholder vote are disclosed; a post-vote Board response was not identified. | Amber |
| Delisting / going-private proposal | No such proposal identified in the reviewed filings. | Green, limited to reviewed filings |

## 5. Minority-Shareholder Protection Read

| Dimension | Read | Evidence-based conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Board oversight | Eight of nine elected directors are classified independent and the chair is independent. | **Favourable structure.** The Burger/BT relationship is a specific commercial-connection monitor, not a demonstrated independence breach. |
| Voice and accountability | Annual elections, majority voting, proxy access and a new 25% special-meeting right support holder voice. | **Adequate.** The 25% threshold and ban on written consent limit practical access for dispersed holders. |
| Change-of-control protections | Advance notice, blank-check preferred-stock authority, vacancy filling and Delaware Section 203 can impede an unsolicited offer. | **Constrained.** No conclusion is made that these tools will be misused. |
| RPT protection | Item 404(a) disclosure is favourable and a review policy is disclosed, but the proxy is outside the frozen set and no matched economic RPT data are available. | **Incomplete evidence.** No “no leakage” conclusion is supported. |
| Shareholder feedback | 41.9% opposition to the stock-plan share increase is a high-severity voting signal; 45.7% support for the political-spending report is also material. | **Requires monitoring.** The sources reviewed do not provide a Board response to either signal. |

**Overall protection read: adequate but constrained.** The structural safeguards are real, but the defence package and the contested stock-plan vote prevent a “strong” conclusion. The biggest evidence limitation remains the frozen pool’s missing proxy, ownership and comprehensive insider-data set. The governance triage specifies that the ownership-data gap caps shareholder friendliness at 60/100; that cap is applied below even though a public SEC proxy was reviewed as supplemental context. [Governance Data Triage, AKAM, 2026-09-14, pp. 11–12 and 19]

| Component | Weight | Raw score | Rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Board structure and independence | 20 | 17 | Independent chair and 8/9 classified independent directors; the two disclosed commercial connections prevent a fully clean independence read. |
| Process, renewal and succession | 15 | 11 | Meeting cadence, evaluation method and refreshment are disclosed; skills mapping, full overboarding and succession outcomes are not. |
| Committee effectiveness | 15 | 12 | Independent Audit Committee, financial expert and meaningful meeting cadence; post-AGM membership and evidence of challenge are incomplete. |

| Rights, corporate actions and AGM voting | 30 | 17 | Annual elections, proxy access and new special-meeting right are offset by written-consent limits, takeover defences and the 41.9% stock-plan opposition. |
| **Raw total** | **100** | **67** | Mixed / adequate structural protection, with material evidence gaps. |
| **Data-sufficiency cap** | — | **60** | Governance triage caps shareholder friendliness at 60 because the frozen pool lacks ownership and comprehensive insider data; the public proxy supplement does not change the frozen input inventory. |
| **Published score** | **100** | **60** | **Mixed. Confidence: 3/5.** |

**Red-flag status:** `RF-SHR-001` is triggered at **High** severity: 41.9% of votes cast opposed the 8.0m-share stock-plan increase. This is not a critical governance flag and does not itself establish misconduct or invalidate the investment. It does require a Board response, stock-plan burn-rate disclosure and a reassessment at the next annual meeting.

# Candor & Disclosure Quality — AKAM

## 1. Owning the Misses

There is no completed management-guidance miss in the available record: Q2 revenue, non-GAAP EPS, and non-GAAP operating margin all landed within the Q1 ranges. The closest adverse communication event is the Q2 update to FY2026 guidance: the revenue high end fell by $20m, non-GAAP EPS high end by $0.10, and the operating-margin outlook moved from about 26% to 25%–26%. The new ranges were publicly reported, but the prepared remarks did not plainly label the changes as reductions or give a complete bridge; readers need to compare the two releases. [Management & Track Record, AKAM, §4; Q1 2026 earnings release, 2026-05-07, p. 2; Q2 2026 earnings release, 2026-08-06, pp. 1–2]

| Miss (from 01) | How It Was Communicated | Owned or Obscured? | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| No completed Q2 2026 management-guide miss: revenue $1,099.682m, non-GAAP EPS $1.59, and non-GAAP operating margin 25% all fell within Q1 ranges | The Q2 release reported each measure and the call stated that the 25% non-GAAP operating margin was in line with management’s expectations. | Owned on the stated non-GAAP guide; this is not evidence of candor through an actual miss. | [Q1 2026 earnings release, Financial guidance, p. 2; Q2 2026 earnings release, Results, p. 1; Q2 2026 earnings call, CFO prepared remarks, p. 6] |
| FY2026 guide narrowed after Q2 — not an actual miss | Q2 presented the new full-year ranges and gave individual drivers including LayerX’s expected $0.12 non-GAAP EPS dilution, lower FX benefit, and investment-led margin pressure. It did not expressly call the $20m revenue-high-end and $0.10 EPS-high-end changes reductions or reconcile the whole change. | Partly owned: the facts were disclosed, but the comparison and full bridge were left to the reader. | [Q1 2026 earnings release, Financial guidance, p. 2; Q2 2026 earnings release, Financial guidance, p. 2; Q2 2026 earnings call, CFO prepared remarks, pp. 6–8] |
| Q2 2026 GAAP profitability decline — not a management-guide miss | The release disclosed GAAP operating income of $80m, down 47%, GAAP operating margin of 7%, down 8 percentage points, and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.52, down 27%. The call instead led profitability commentary with non-GAAP net income and margin. | Partly owned: reported in the release, but given less weight in spoken management framing. | [Q2 2026 earnings release, Results, pp. 1–2; Q2 2026 earnings call, CFO prepared remarks, p. 6] |

## 2. Non-GAAP / Adjustment Aggressiveness

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Recurring "one-off" addbacks | FY2025 non-GAAP results excluded $459.4m of stock-based compensation (SBC), exceeding FY2025 GAAP net income of $452.0m. Restructuring charges were $56.6m, $95.4m, and $58.1m in FY2023–FY2025; H1 2026 also included $275.0m of SBC and $2.0m of restructuring charges. | [Q2 2026 Supplemental Financial Information, GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliation sheet, FY2023–H1 2026 columns; Earnings Quality, AKAM, §§4–5] |
| GAAP-to-adjusted gap (magnitude / trend) | In Q2 2026, GAAP operating income was $80.3m versus non-GAAP operating income of $270.7m: a $190.4m adjustment, or 237% of GAAP operating income. FY2025’s $686.7m operating-income adjustment was 121% of GAAP operating income ($1,253.6m non-GAAP versus $566.9m GAAP). | [Q2 2026 Supplemental Financial Information, GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliation sheet, Q2 2026 and FY2025 columns; Earnings Quality, AKAM, §§4, 7] |
| Does adjusted framing flatter reality? | Yes. The reconciliation is disclosed, so the presentation is not hidden; however, it removes recurring employee pay, recurring restructuring, and acquired-intangible amortization. The Q2 release therefore showed non-GAAP EPS of $1.59 beside GAAP EPS of $0.52, a $1.07 difference. | [Q2 2026 earnings release, Results, pp. 1–2; Q2 2026 Supplemental Financial Information, Non-GAAP Definitions and GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliation sheets] |

## 3. Disclosure Transparency

The releases give usable decision data: GAAP and non-GAAP results are shown side by side, the reconciliation is itemized, and revenue is broken into Security, Delivery and other cloud applications, and Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS). [Q2 2026 earnings release, 2026-08-06, pp. 1–2; Q2 2026 Supplemental Financial Information, GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliation sheet] The solution-category KPI is only newly reported from Q1 2026, although prior FY2025 quarters were recast; this improves visibility into CIS but does not establish five years of stable KPI reporting. There is no evidence in the available record that a KPI was dropped or redefined after deterioration, so this is an Amber comparability limit, not RF-MGT-003. [Q1 2026 Supplemental Financial Information, Supplemental Revenue sheet; Q2 2026 Supplemental Financial Information, Supplemental Revenue sheet]

## 4. Tone in Bad Times

Q2 is the weakest current period available: the release disclosed the GAAP earnings and margin decline while the CFO also directly named Delivery and other cloud applications revenue down 6%, higher colocation, depreciation and headcount costs, and an expected step-up in capex. [Q2 2026 earnings release, Results, pp. 1–2; Q2 2026 earnings call, CFO prepared remarks, pp. 6–8] The CEO’s opening was heavily promotional about AI contracts and third-party recognition, but in Q&A the CFO answered revenue timing, cost pass-through, pre-revenue colocation costs, and the GPU-delivery slip; notably, he said CIS growth should not accelerate in Q3 before a projected Q4 ramp. No direct numerical contradiction between the management commentary and the disclosed results was identified in the two available verbatim 2026 calls. [Q2 2026 earnings call, CEO prepared remarks, pp. 4–5; CFO Q&A, pp. 9–14]

## 5. Candor Read

**Mixed.** Management does put the adverse operating facts and revised ranges into the public record and gives direct, useful answers on the timing and cost of the CIS build-out. But the economic earnings picture is made materially better by excluding recurring SBC and repeat restructuring charges, while the prepared-message tone gives much more space to AI validation than to falling GAAP profitability.

The single biggest candor signal is the reconciliation itself: FY2025 SBC of $459.4m exceeded GAAP net income of $452.0m, and Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating income was $270.7m versus $80.3m on a GAAP basis. This is aggressive adjusted framing, not evidence that the disclosed GAAP figures are false. [Q2 2026 Supplemental Financial Information, GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliation sheet, FY2025 and Q2 2026 columns]

RF-DISC-002 (recurring "one-off" / aggressive non-GAAP add-backs)

## 6. Provenance & Next Request

### Source use

- **Tier 1 / primary frozen evidence:** FY25 Form 10-K, Q1/Q2 FY26 Forms 10-Q, including the FY25 Exhibit 21.1 subsidiary listing and the statement that Items 10–14 are incorporated from the proxy.
- **Tier 1 / primary public regulator sweep:** SEC EDGAR 2026 DEF 14A, filed 2026-03-31. Used for the current roster, disclosed outside roles and Item 404/family-relationship read. It is not represented as part of the frozen pool.
- **Company source:** Akamai’s company-history and company/IR pages. The history page was German original and translated faithfully for lineage; it is self-disclosed, so it is not used to prove legal registry facts.
- **Tier 5 vendor inputs:** CIQ facts sidecar and Capital IQ Suppliers/Customers relationship graph. The ownership export was missing; the relationship graph had zero rows and expressly does not cover the full group/related-party universe.
- **Public legal-database sweep:** SEC enforcement, DOJ, CourtListener and OpenSanctions scoped web queries. “No attributable hit identified” is a sweep-log result only; it is not proof of a clean record.

**Single highest-value next request:** Add the filed **2026 DEF 14A**, including its ownership/pledge, compensation, Item 404 and director/officer disclosure sections, to the frozen evidence generation; then provide a named KMP roster including the Chief Security Officer.

## 7. People & Network Integrity Read

**Verdict: Coverage-limited — no disqualifying or material personal-integrity fact identified from completed checks.**

The strongest positive fact is the public SEC proxy’s explicit statement of no 2025 Item 404(a) transactions and no family relationships among the named executive officers/directors, while Akamai has a separate independent chair. The key limitation is not a proven issue at a person or entity: it is the evidence boundary. The frozen pool omitted the proxy incorporated into the FY25 10-K, CIQ ownership data are missing, the relationship graph is empty and critical registry/court checks could not be completed. This caps the people-and-network score at 65/100 and confidence at 70/100.

**Monitor items:** (1) confirm Ahola’s Nasdaq council recusal/conflict controls; (2) reconcile Noname Gate Ltd. versus Noname Security Ltd.; (3) identify the unnamed Chief Security Officer; and (4) replace the coverage-limited public searches with identity-anchored official records.

# Audit & Assurance Quality — AKAM

## 1. The Assurance Stack

| Role | Firm / Person | Network | Signing partner | Appointed | Tenure (yrs) | Local cap | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Statutory auditor | PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (Boston; PCAOB ID 238) | PwC | Not named in the FY2025 10-K. The available PCAOB Form AP result identifies Paul F. Dinunzio for FY2019, not the FY2025 audit; it is not evidence of the current partner. | Served since 1998 | 28 at FY2025 | U.S.: no mandatory firm-rotation cap; lead-partner rotation must be checked separately | [FY2025 Form 10-K, p.52; PCAOB Form AP, Akamai FY2019 audit, filed 2020-03-19] |
| Principal component auditors | Not disclosed | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.51–52; Exhibit 21.1] |
| Internal auditor | Not disclosed | Not assessable | Not applicable | Not assessable | Not assessable | U.S. issuer; no India-style secretarial-audit regime | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Items 8 and 9A] |
| Secretarial auditor (India) | Not applicable — U.S. SEC issuer | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | MR-3 / secretarial audit is not a U.S. requirement | [FY2025 Form 10-K, cover; Item 8] |

The firm’s 28-year tenure is not itself a U.S. rotation breach: U.S. rules rotate the lead engagement partner, not necessarily the audit firm. The frozen record does not identify the FY2025 partner or provide the current Form AP result, so the lead-partner rotation test is not proven.

## 2. Opinions, Controls & Restatements (A4-05, A4-09, A7-02)

| FY | Opinion (standalone) | Opinion (consolidated) | EoM / going concern | IFC/ICFR opinion | Restatement / prior-period adjustment | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | Not applicable — the supplied U.S. filing reports consolidated statements, not a separate parent-only audit | PwC’s FY2025 report audits the FY2023 income, comprehensive-income, equity and cash-flow statements as comparative periods | None stated in the FY2025 report | Current-year ICFR opinion only | Separate FY2023 annual report / Item 4.02 history absent | Green for the comparative statements; five-year restatement history not proven | [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.51–52] |
| 2024 | Not applicable — same U.S. consolidated reporting basis | Unqualified; FY2024 consolidated balance sheet audited in the FY2025 report | None stated | Current-year ICFR opinion only | Separate FY2024 annual report / Item 4.02 history absent | Green for the comparative balance sheet; five-year restatement history not proven | [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.51–52] |
| 2025 | Not applicable — same U.S. consolidated reporting basis | Unqualified: presents fairly in all material respects under U.S. GAAP | No emphasis-of-matter or going-concern paragraph stated | Unqualified/effective ICFR opinion as of 2025-12-31 | Cover says no error correction and no Rule 10D-1 recovery-analysis restatement | Green current opinion and controls; restatement sweep remains incomplete | [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.51–52; cover] |

The business-model disqualifier scan says verbatim: **“No disqualifier triggered.”** Its auditor row reports PwC’s unqualified FY2025 financial-statement and ICFR opinions, with no stated going-concern paragraph; no hard-lock deference is therefore active. [business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md, §§1–3]

| A4-01 — tenure vs local cap; rotation real? | PwC has served since 1998 (28 years at FY2025). No U.S. firm-rotation cap applies; current engagement partner and partner tenure are not disclosed/retrieved. The only identified Form AP partner is Paul F. ## 10. Read

**Assurance mixed — watch the independence and coverage evidence.** PwC issued an unqualified FY2025 consolidated and ICFR opinion covering the supplied FY2023–FY2025 statements, and the firm says it has served since 1998; that supports the current reported numbers. But the fee split, current engagement partner, partner-rotation evidence, component-audit coverage and audit-committee session detail are absent, while PwC U.S. has a documented 2024 PCAOB independence-quality-control sanction unrelated to AKAM; the FY2026 DEF 14A plus the current PCAOB Form AP are the minimum needed to trust the assurance chain more fully.

# Related-Party & Group Forensics — AKAM

**As of:** 2026-09-14  
**Basis:** U.S. GAAP; USD millions unless stated. `data/AKAM/` below is a logical label for the frozen evidence generation. The FY25 proxy that the 10-K incorporates for Item 13 is absent from that generation. A completed upstream public-EDGAR read of the 2026 DEF 14A is used only with that limitation stated.

## 1. RPT Intensity & the Applicable Regime (A5-01)

Applicable materiality rule per period: Akamai is a Delaware/Nasdaq issuer. For FY2023–FY2025, the relevant related-person disclosure rule is SEC Item 404(a): transactions above the $120,000 disclosure floor in which a covered related person had a direct or indirect material interest. This is a disclosure test, not an aggregate-RPT materiality test. The India LODR Reg. 23 slabs do not apply.

| FY | Aggregate RPTs ex-dividends | % of revenue | % of PAT | % of assets | Material-RPT line that year | Above the line? | Minority-approved? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | Not assessable — no Item 404/RPT disclosure in the frozen pool | N/A | N/A | N/A | SEC Item 404(a), $120k disclosure floor | Not assessable | Not assessable | Insufficient Data | [FY25 Form 10-K, Item 13, p.95 — incorporates absent 2026 proxy] |
| 2024 | Not assessable — no Item 404/RPT disclosure in the frozen pool | N/A | N/A | N/A | SEC Item 404(a), $120k disclosure floor | Not assessable | Not assessable | Insufficient Data | [FY25 Form 10-K, Item 13, p.95 — incorporates absent 2026 proxy] |
| 2025 | 0 Item 404(a)-reportable transactions; this is **not** a full aggregate-RPT ledger | N/A — do not divide the zero disclosure count by revenue | N/A | N/A | SEC Item 404(a), $120k disclosure floor | No Item 404(a) transaction reported | U.S. minority-vote approval not evidenced in supplied sources | Amber | [2026 DEF 14A, p.39 — public EDGAR read recorded in 07 People & Network Integrity Dossiers §4; proxy not in frozen pool] |

FY25 revenue was $4,208.175m, GAAP net income (PAT) $452.031m and total assets $11,479.643m, but no aggregate RPT amount exists to use as a numerator. A $0 Item 404 disclosure count cannot be relabelled as “0% RPTs.” [FY25 Form 10-K, pp.53–54; 2026 DEF 14A, p.39 — cross-module public EDGAR read]

The reported amount does not exceed 25% of revenue or expenses because no reported amount exists. The >25% hard-lock test therefore **defers to** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`, which records the ratio as not assessable and does not trigger the lock. [business-model/01_disqualifier-scan, §§1 and 4]

## 2. The RPT Ledger (every named counterparty)

The named-counterparty universe built from the available RPT sources is empty: the upstream public-proxy read reports no FY25 Item 404(a) transaction, while FY23–FY24 proxy/RPT disclosures are absent. This is not evidence that Akamai had no intercompany or below-threshold transactions.

| Counterparty | Relationship | Type (sales/purchases/royalty/rent/loan/guarantee/other) | FY-2 | FY-1 | FY (latest) | Trend | Arm's-length basis disclosed? | Source |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| No named related-party counterparty disclosed in supplied RPT materials | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | 0 Item 404(a) rows, not a dollar ledger | Not assessable | Not assessable | [2026 DEF 14A, p.39 — cross-module public EDGAR read; FY25 Form 10-K, Item 13, p.95] |

## 3. Promoter-Linked Channels

### 3A. Royalty / brand / technology fees (A5-02)

| Payee | What is provided | Amount | % of turnover | Basis disclosed? | Trend vs margins | Prior minority approval? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| No promoter/group payee identified | Brand/technology fee cannot be tested without the Item 404 policy and RPT note | N/A | N/A | Not assessable | Not assessable | Not assessable | Insufficient Data | [FY25 Form 10-K, Item 13, p.95; 07 People & Network Integrity Dossiers, §§4–5] |

The network read has not verified the owner of Akamai or product trademarks, including the former LayerX product branding. External ownership, a controller link, a licence, and any fee are all unproven; RF-NET-004 does not fire on that unresolved ownership question alone. [07 People & Network Integrity Dossiers, §§0A, 5; A17-04]

### 3B. Loans / ICDs / guarantees to the group (A5-03)

| Instrument | Counterparty | Amount | Rate vs market | Rolled over? | Counterparty health (registry) | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loans, intercompany deposits (ICDs) or guarantees to a promoter/related entity | No RPT note or legal-entity cash ledger supplied | N/A | N/A | Not assessable | Not assessable | Insufficient Data | [FY25 Form 10-K, Item 13, p.95; 07 People & Network Integrity Dossiers, §5] |

The company’s standard third-party indemnities are not identified as related-party guarantees. Their fair value was immaterial in FY25 and H1 FY26, but this does not quantify any group guarantee; any future group guarantee belongs also in `10_contingent-liabilities-and-commitments` (A7a-06), counted once. [FY25 Form 10-K, Item 7 Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements, p.45; Q2 FY26 Form 10-Q, Item 2 Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements, p.42]

### 3C. Promoter-vendor / promoter-customer flows (A5-04)

| Entity | Customer / vendor / both | Value | % of revenue or COGS | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Unnamed affiliate of a large social-media customer | Customer-side affiliate; **not** identified as an Akamai promoter, director or KMP entity | FY25 sublease income $8.187m; corresponding operating plus variable lease cost $8.033m | Income 0.195% of FY25 revenue; cost 0.191% | Not an RPT on available evidence; named-person link and legal name are absent | [FY25 Form 10-K, Note 12, pp.79–80; FY25 Form 10-K, p.54] |
| Promoter-linked vendor/customer | None identified in the available records | N/A | N/A | Insufficient Data — missing RPT ledger prevents a complete test | [FY25 Form 10-K, Item 13, p.95; 2026 DEF 14A, p.39 — cross-module public EDGAR read] |

The data-centre sublease has an identifiable commercial purpose and was close to flat in FY25: $8.187m income less $6.959m operating cost and $1.074m variable cost equals $0.154m net income. That arithmetic does not establish an arm’s-length related-party transaction; it instead shows why the unnamed customer affiliate should not be falsely placed in the RPT ledger. [FY25 Form 10-K, Note 12, pp.79–80]

## 4. Round-Tripping Cross-Year Name Match (A5-04)

One list was built across every available period: FY23–FY24 contain no supplied Item 404/RPT disclosure; FY25’s upstream proxy read contains zero Item 404(a) counterparties; the Capital IQ Suppliers/Customers graph contains zero named rows and explicitly is not a complete group or supplier-base view. Therefore no named customer-vendor match can be tested.

| Name | Years as customer | Years as vendor | Both roles? | Sales ≈ purchases (circular)? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No named RPT counterparties | N/A | N/A | Not assessable | Not assessable | Amber — investigation cannot be completed from an empty name list | [2026 DEF 14A, p.39 — cross-module public EDGAR read; Capital IQ Suppliers/Customers graph, frozen 2026-09-14 — tier-5, zero rows and scope-limited] |

No circularity conclusion is drawn. A two-way commercial match would be Amber until mirrored amounts/timing, off-market pricing, or a funds-flow circle supported a Red conclusion.

## 14. Read

No dollar flow from Akamai to a promoter/controller group is proven. The only current direct evidence is an upstream public-proxy read of zero FY25 Item 404(a) transactions; it is not an aggregate RPT number, so the transaction intensity and % of PAT cannot be measured. The group has 46 listed subsidiaries and no disclosed cash-by-entity chart; that structure can obscure leakage if it exists, while the 46 count alone does not prove it does. The highest-value missing disclosure is the frozen 2026 DEF 14A Item 404 policy/transaction table plus the legal-entity ownership and intercompany cash/loan ledger.

# Contingent Liabilities & Commitments — AKAM

All figures are USD millions under U.S. GAAP. The latest balance-sheet point is 30 June 2026, but the latest full commitments schedule and tax-reserve detail are at 31 December 2025. The frozen pool has the FY2025 Form 10-K and FY2026 interim filings, not separate FY2023 or FY2024 annual reports; the three-year income-tax-reserve series is nevertheless disclosed in the FY2025 tax note. `balance-sheet-survival/05_off-balance-sheet-and-contingencies.md` was available and is used for its exposure totals; this report adds the disclosure, movement, and provisioning read rather than rebuilding those totals.

## 1. Headline Exposure (A7a-01)

| Measure | Amount | Denominator (figure + source) | % | Band (Green <5% NW / Red >25% NW or >50% PAT) | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Quantified tax-audit reserve (unrecognized tax benefits plus accrued interest and penalties) | $111.4 | Net worth = $4,977.4 [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.53] | 2.2% | Green by net-worth size | Green on size; audit posture is not disclosed | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 19 (Income Taxes), pp.89–90] |
| All non-lease contingencies | Not aggregable: standard indemnities are unlimited; purchase commitments and litigation claims are unquantified | Net worth = $4,977.4 [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.53] | Not meaningful | Cannot test | Insufficient Data — absence of a cap is not a measured loss | [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 13 (Commitments and Contingencies), pp.80–81] |
| Known gross lease-related commitments — $1,865.9 scheduled payments + $278.0 uncommenced co-location leases + $187.1 final data-centre commitment | $2,331.0 | Net worth = $4,977.4 [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets, p.53] | 46.8% | Red | Red financial materiality; $1,570.0 of operating-lease liabilities was already recognized, so this is not $2,331.0 of unprovided contingent loss | [balance-sheet-survival/05_off-balance-sheet-and-contingencies.md, §4; FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 12 (Leases), pp.79–80] |
| Known gross lease-related commitments | $2,331.0 | FY2025 PAT = $452.0 [FY2025 Form 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income, p.54] | 515.7% | Red; commitment stock versus one-year profit flow, so not a loss forecast | Red financial materiality | [balance-sheet-survival/05_off-balance-sheet-and-contingencies.md, §4; FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 12 (Leases), pp.79–80] |

The $2,331.0 commitment total is a disclosed gross figure, not a net cash burden or an off-P&L provision. It includes $560.3 of scheduled data-centre sublease payments and the $187.1 final portion that commenced in January 2026; the filing separately expects $731.2 of future sublease income through 2034/2037, which is not netted in the total. This size breaches the module’s materiality trigger on a gross commitment basis (RF-FIN-003 and RF-CL-001, High), but the qualifier matters: most of the contractual obligation is already a recognized lease liability and a portion is expected to be offset by sublease income. [FY2025 Form 10-K, Note 12 (Leases), p.80; balance-sheet-survival/05_off-balance-sheet-and-contingencies.md, §§1 and 4]

## 11. Read

The only quantified non-lease contingency is the $111.4 tax-audit reserve, 2.2% of FY2025 net worth of $4,977.4, and it is provided for; the filing does not show serial appeal losses or a tax demand that would make that reserve a Red item. The largest known contractual exposure is instead $2,331.0 of gross lease-related payments and uncommenced commitments, 46.8% of the same-date net worth; $1,570.0 was already recognized as lease liabilities and $731.2 of future sublease income is disclosed separately, so this is material but not a $2,331.0 unprovided loss. Management is reasonably candid on lease detail, tax-reserve movements, and the unlimited nature of indemnities, but it does not quantify purchase commitments, litigation claims, bills with recourse, bank guarantees, or group-entity contingencies. A rational minority holder should watch the next annual lease schedule, the unquantified bandwidth/purchase commitments supporting cloud expansion, and any named tax or litigation matter; no court or tribunal database sweep was run because the filings do not identify the largest disputed matters, so all posture statements are filings-only.

# Accounting Forensics — AKAM

All amounts are USD millions unless stated otherwise. Akamai is a U.S. GAAP cybersecurity and cloud-services issuer with a 31 December year-end; it is not a bank, NBFC, or insurer, so the normal accrual batteries apply. This report uses the frozen evidence set only. The FY2025 10-K contains audited FY2025/FY2024 balance-sheet comparatives and FY2023–FY2025 income and cash-flow comparatives; the source-bound Capital IQ workbook supplies the FY2023 balance-sheet date needed solely for the Dechow opening-balance arithmetic.

## 2. Beneish M-Score (A8-14) — computed with Python 3.12, computation shown

The Beneish M-score is a statistical screen for earnings-manipulation patterns, not a fraud finding. Calculation used the audited input table and `M = −4.84 + 0.920·DSRI + 0.528·GMI + 0.404·AQI + 0.892·SGI + 0.115·DEPI − 0.172·SGAI − 0.327·LVGI + 4.679·TATA`.

| Component | Value FY2025 | Non-manipulator mean | Manipulator zone | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| DSRI (receivables outrunning sales) | 1.034 | 1.031 | ≥1.465 | Green |
| GMI (gross margin deteriorating) | 1.007 | 1.014 | ≥1.193 | Green |
| AQI (asset quality softening) | 1.194 | 1.039 | ≥1.254 | Green |
| SGI (sales growth pressure) | 1.054 | 1.134 | ≥1.607 | Green |
| DEPI (depreciation rate slowing) | 1.069 | 1.001 | ≥1.077 | Green |
| SGAI (overhead vs sales) | 0.991 | 1.054 | not banded (negative weight in M) | Green |
| LVGI (leverage rising) | 1.021 | 1.037 | ≥1.111 | Green |
| TATA (accruals vs assets) | −0.093 | 0.018 | ≥0.031 | Green |

`M = −4.84 + 0.920(1.034) + 0.528(1.007) + 0.404(1.194) + 0.892(1.054) + 0.115(1.069) − 0.172(0.991) − 0.327(1.021) + 4.679(−0.093) = −2.750`.

| Composite / rule | Value | Green band | Amber band | Red band | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| M-score | −2.750 | < −2.22, no component in zone | −2.22 to −1.78 (re-check drivers) | > −1.78 | Green |
| Components in manipulator zone | 0 of 7 banded | 0 | 1–2 (Amber — the composite decides) | ≥3 | Green |

## 3. Dechow F-Score & Accrual Battery (A8-17, A8-18) — computed with Python 3.12, computation shown

The Dechow F-score is a misstatement-probability screen where 1.00 is the average-company level. Using the model definitions, average FY2024/FY2025 assets are $10,924.214m. RSST accruals — balance-sheet accruals across working capital, non-current operations and financing — are −2.870%: working capital moved $39.307m to $132.629m, non-current operating assets $6,512.686m to $7,030.336m, and net financial assets $(2,191.343)m to $(3,115.825)m. Cash sales are $4,142.196m in FY2025 and $3,987.783m in FY2024; the FY2024 figure uses the frozen FY2023 receivables comparative. `pred = −5.4398`, probability = 0.4322%, and `F = 0.004322 / 0.0037 = 1.168`.

| Test | Value | Green band | Red band | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Dechow F-score (1.00 = average company) | 1.168 | <1.00 | ≥1.85 (substantial; ≥2.45 high) | Amber | [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.53–56; Capital IQ Financials workbook, Balance Sheet FY2023] |
| RSST accruals / average assets | −2.87% | ≤3% | ≥10% | Green | [FY2025 Form 10-K, p.53; Capital IQ Financials workbook, Balance Sheet FY2023; calculation shown above] |
| Soft assets % of total assets | 71.57%; down from 75.72% | <50% | >65% and rising | Amber — high but falling | [FY2025 Form 10-K, p.53; calculation from cited rows] |
| Δ receivables / average assets | 0.60% | <2% | ≥5% with no acquisition explaining it | Green | [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.53–54; calculation] |
| Δ inventory / average assets | 0.00% (no inventory line reported) | <2% | ≥5% with no acquisition explaining it | Green | [FY2025 Form 10-K, p.53] |
| A8-18 — issuance in a flagged year | $1.725bn convertible issuance; F <1.85 and TATA −9.29% | none while flagged; self-funded | issued while F ≥1.85 or TATA ≥0.031 (RF-ACC-004) | Green — issuance was not in an accrual-flagged year | [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.54–56; Note 11, p.75] |

The F-score is Amber because soft assets are 71.57% of assets, not because accruals, receivables, inventory or the composite cleared a red band. The asset-mix figure is high but fell 415 basis points year on year, so it does not meet the stated “high and rising” red condition. No RF-ACC-001 or RF-ACC-004 is triggered.

## 12. Forensics Read

The measured manipulation screens are not red: Beneish M is −2.750 with zero component-zone hits, and Dechow F is 1.168, below the 1.85 substantial-misstatement threshold. The closest measured concern is the 71.57% soft-asset share that makes the F-score Amber, although it fell from 75.72%; cash authenticity cannot be confirmed by a yield test because the disclosed interest line is mixed. A rational minority holder should treat the books as cash-backed on the reported CFO measures, but not treat management’s adjusted profit as equivalent to economic earnings while recurring restructuring, rising capitalized SBC and strict leverage of 5.14x remain open risks.

# Regulatory, Legal & Compliance — AKAM

**Scope and evidence boundary.** This is a 2026-09-14 public-record sweep for Akamai Technologies, Inc. (Nasdaq: AKAM; CIK 0001086222). Frozen company filings are cited logically as `data/AKAM/`. SEC, DOJ, company, agency, court-search, exchange, sanctions and adverse-media queries were run where reachable; PACER, a complete Nasdaq disciplinary archive, the Israeli Companies Registrar and Israeli primary court docket were not independently downloaded. Thus, a search result of no attributable matter is a coverage observation, not proof of absence. The $5% net-worth screen used below is $237.4m, calculated as 5% of $4,748.5m common equity at 2026-06-30. [FY2026 Q2 Form 10-Q, balance sheet]

## 9. Read

**Hygiene lapses, watch.** The filings' generic statement that legal matters are routine is not contradicted by a confirmed current material enforcement case, but it omits the useful historical context: a 2016 SEC non-prosecution agreement over China-related improper-payment conduct and a 2013 former-employee insider-trading settlement. The hotline and Audit Committee review look real as mechanisms, but the company does not publish complaint volumes or outcomes. The single most decision-relevant current item is not a legal fine: third-party sources report two S&P downgrades within 54 days and a negative outlook, while the full agency records and lender syndicate still need confirmation; this is a watch item, not a legal/regulatory verdict cap.

# AKAM — Valuation synthesis (corrected 2026-09-15)

## 1. Verdict and ownership

**Materially overvalued on the stated conditional cash model, low confidence.** This is a targeted integrity correction of the September 14 publication. It does not establish an empirically calibrated cost of capital or refresh all company research. Raw valuation confidence remains 50/100; the master applies a cumulative ten-point adversarial haircut for 40/100 effective conviction. Valuation attractiveness 10/100, margin-of-safety score 5/100, downside risk 85/100 (inverted: higher is worse), data quality 72/100 and usefulness 62/100 are retained judgments. No rating upgrade follows from repairing arithmetic.

## 2. Adjudicated valuation

The corrected common-basis 12-month distribution is joint bull $153.392526 (10%), sensitivity bull $113.616526 (15%), base $71.263910 (45%) and cyclical bear $47.295374 (30%). Weighted target $78.639103 and expected return −26.360986% reconcile. All probabilities are judgment. The cash model is the only weighted method; its 82.8493% terminal-value share and proxy construction keep it weak evidence for a precise value. The $35.21738 structural check is a separate 24–36 month floor and receives no 12-month probability weight.

## 3. What changed

GAAP diluted shares 153.686m include 5.353m convertible dilution whose economic note-hedge benefit was omitted. Subtracting it gives 148.333m working shares, while retaining cash-settled principal in debt. Forward and reverse models now use the same working denominator. The $106.79 quote therefore targets synthetic working-basis EV $21,923.05207m. The current observed market EV is still $21,428.294m on 143.700m current shares; these are different bases and are labeled. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7 pp.18–20; Note 13 p.25; MD&A p.39; Capital IQ Comps Financial Data, 2026-09-14]

The Treasury 4.83% September 9 input and Damodaran January 2026 4.23% ERP are now source-bound. Beta 1.00 is an explicit assumption; no unverified raw beta is used. Debt cost is a historical accounting-interest proxy and the weights use carrying debt. The 6.216848% blend is consequently a conditional model assumption. The September 14 Treasury update and realistic-debt-cost hypotheses are shown as sensitivities in 04, not suppressed.

## 4. Contrary evidence and falsification

The matched reverse growth is 16.9744503%, or alternatively a 4.9553250% implied rate on base cash. Both are model inferences. The combination gives a +43.64% joint bull, so the distribution spans material upside. Security/CIS commitments could improve cash conversion rapidly; a point-in-time diluted reconstruction or a genuinely independent matched valuation could weaken Avoid. By Q2 FY2027, test same-basis LTM FCF against approximately $736.8m and seek improving GAAP margins. An independent warranted peer value at or above the market would challenge the sole weighted DCF.

## 5. Peer and SOTP adjudication

The original own-history six-close sample and heterogeneous peer median retain zero weight. Additional Cloudflare, Fortinet and Fastly workbooks exist in the September 15 extract; this correction does not falsely call them absent, nor treat their existence as a completed matched valuation. SOTP remains not assessable because filed category profit, invested capital and cash conversion are missing. No old mechanical peer price is a valid fair value. The next request is a complete matched peer valuation, including a consistent enterprise-value bridge and forward metric definitions, rather than just another target-price opinion.

## 6. Decision and limits

The negative conditional expected return supports rejecting a long at $106.79 while awaiting those tests. It does not support a Short Candidate: upside is material and borrow/options data are absent. The serial-acquisition Watchlist ceiling and governance forensic cap are retained from the dedicated modules and not averaged away. A distress lock is not invented: the balance-sheet module says Adequate, with numerical covenant headroom not assessable.

## 7. Audit trail

01 owns price/debt/hedges/shares; 04 owns the full equations, source-bound rate inputs and sensitivities; 05 owns the matched reverse solve; 07 owns probabilities and returns. `corrected_model.json` preserves precision and `reproduce_model.py` reproduces it. The final master and record carry the same four cases. The new audits bind final exact bytes; original reports, audits and admission remain immutable in analyses/AKAM_2026-09-14.

## 6. Sufficiency Verdict

- **Verdict:** Sufficient
- **Reason:** The pool contains usable FY/LTM income and cash-flow bases, a current balance sheet and debt data, dated pool-verified price and peer multiples, plus forward consensus and guidance; this supports more than two valid methods.
- **Methods that can run:** own-history multiples (limited history), peer relative valuation, intrinsic FCFF DCF, and reverse-DCF.
- **Critical implementation limitation:** The CIQ own-history multiples series has only six quarterly closes, so it may be a cross-check but cannot be treated as a stable 3–5-year reversion anchor. The estimates export also lacks an explicit snapshot date inside the workbook; its content is usable, but downstream agents must carry that freshness qualification.

> Targeted correction published 2026-09-15. Operating forecasts and the $106.79 price remain dated 2026-09-14. This report replaces the affected valuation output; unaffected modules are reused with lineage in `maintenance_lineage.json`. No new specialist execution is claimed.

# AKAM — Price, debt and economic share anchor

## 1. Decision price and capitalization

The Capital IQ Comps Financial Data worksheet reports price **$106.79** and current shares **143.700m**, as of 2026-09-14. Their product is current market capitalization **$15,345.723m**. These vendor observations are not filing numbers. [Capital IQ Comps, Financial Data, Day Close Price Latest and Shares Outstanding Latest, 2026-09-14; canonical ciq_facts.json]

## 2. Debt and cash bridge

| Item | USD millions | Source / meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Convertible debt carrying amount | 7,562.828 | Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7, p.19 |
| Convertible cash principal | 7,640.000 | Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7, pp.17–19 |
| Cash and equivalents | 1,480.257 | Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, balance sheet, p.3 |
| **Strict net debt, carrying basis** | **6,082.571** | 7,562.828 − 1,480.257; no securities netted |
| Principal less cash sensitivity | 6,159.743 | 7,640.000 − 1,480.257 |
| Debt fair value | 8,674.998 | Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7, p.19; includes embedded conversion economics |
| Current market EV, strict carrying bridge | 21,428.294 | 15,345.723 + 6,082.571 |

The filing requires settlement of principal in cash on conversion, with value above principal paid in cash or shares. Therefore a share correction does not justify removing all convertible debt. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7, p.18]

## 3. Economic diluted working shares

GAAP Q2 diluted weighted-average shares are **153.686m = 144.660m basic + 3.673m stock awards + 5.353m note conversion dilution**. GAAP EPS excludes the purchased note-hedge benefit. The filing separately shows the **5.353m** hedge adjustment in its economic/non-GAAP diluted share reconciliation. Subtracting that matched benefit gives **148.333m** economic diluted working shares. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 13, p.25; Note 7, pp.19–20; MD&A non-GAAP diluted-share reconciliation, p.39]

This is a period-average working count, not a verified point-in-time fully diluted count. The 3.673m award dilution is the disclosed period treasury-stock-method result. Current award quantities and strike details are insufficient for an exact September 14 reconstruction. Purchased hedges offset note-conversion premiums; sold warrants are separate. The lowest disclosed warrant strike is $155.02, above all four canonical scenario prices. Any scenario above a warrant strike must include its incremental claim. The calculation artifact solves that claim explicitly rather than assuming all future dilution is zero. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Note 7, pp.19–20]

## 4. Anchor Block

Forward fair values and reverse solves use **148.333m** economic working shares and **$6,082.571m** strict net debt. At $106.79, the reverse model must target **$15,840.48107m equity = 106.79 × 148.333**, and **$21,923.05207m enterprise value**. This is a synthetic value on the working diluted basis, not current observed market capitalization. The observed 143.700m shares remain valid for current market cap only. Mixing its $21,428.294m EV with 148.333m fair-value shares would fail to reproduce the quoted price.

Using principal rather than carrying debt lowers every below-strike price by **$0.520262 = (7,640.000 − 7,562.828) / 148.333**. This does not reverse the decision. The filing's debt fair value is disclosed but is not silently substituted into the bridge without matching the purchased hedge and embedded conversion-option valuation.

The price is $106.79 at 14 September 2026; the canonical enterprise value (EV, market value plus debt less cash) is $21,428.3m, and the diluted per-share working count is 153.686m. [valuation/01_price-and-capital-structure, §§1, 4, 7]

[Capital IQ Financials → Multiples, Close rows, 2025-03-31 to 2026-09-11; source-bound `ciq_facts.json`, `ev_ebitda_current_x` = 13.4, `ev_ebitda_percentile` = 0.833, and `range_position`, present]

## 3. Re-Rating / De-Rating Read

On the more comparable equity measures, P/LTM EPS is 38.8x, 28.4% above its six-quarter mean of 30.2x and 44.4% above its 26.9x median: `(38.7810 − 30.2111) / 30.2111` and `(38.7810 − 26.8516) / 26.8516`. P/NTM normalized EPS is 15.6x, 11.9% above its 13.9x mean and 20.5% above its 12.9x median; P/B is 3.23x, 14.4% and 24.4% above its 2.82x mean and 2.60x median. [Capital IQ Financials → Multiples, `P/LTM EPS`, `P/NTM EPS`, and `P/BV` Close rows, 2025-03-31 to 2026-09-11]

The vendor TEV/LTM EBITDA series is also 21.3% above its 11.0x mean and 32.4% above its 10.1x median, but it is a lower-confidence confirmation because its EV and EBITDA definitions do not reconcile to the canonical filing-based calculation in §1. The change cannot be causally proven from the available data. Inference, not from filings: the market is giving some credit to the security/cloud mix — management guides CIS growth of at least 50% and high-single-digit Security growth in FY2026 — while the counter-evidence is lower LTM margins and much higher strict net debt. [Capital IQ Financials → Multiples, `TEV/LTM EBITDA` Close row, 2025-03-31 to 2026-09-11; Q2 2026 earnings call, CFO prepared remarks; earnings/01_historical-financials, §§2, 6; valuation/01_price-and-capital-structure, §5]

## 4. Implied Value from Reversion

No own-history implied EV, equity value, or per-share target is published. A six-observation, 1.5-year history is below the roughly three-year minimum for a mean/median reversion target, and the vendor EV/EBITDA, EV/EBIT, and levered-FCF series do not have a complete bridge to the filing-based strict-EV and GAAP measures. Any price derived from those medians would be illustrative-only and is not a fair-value input for `07_scenario-and-fair-value`.

The required base-case own-history implied value is therefore **Not assessable**. The evidence supports a directional conclusion — current P/E, P/B, and vendor EV multiples are in the upper half of this short sample — but not a point or tight reversion range. A reversion calculation would additionally assume the warranted multiple is unchanged. That assumption is not supported: Q2 gross margin was 55.8%, down 331 basis points year on year, and strict net debt was $6.08bn, up from $3.18bn at FY2025. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Statements of Income, p.5; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, pp.3–4; earnings/01_historical-financials, §§1–2]

## 5. Sector Cycle Reality Test

No material same-direction sector move is indicated over the available short window: IGV, an ETF tracking North American software and related digital-media companies, rose from $88.97 in March 2025 to $101.52 in September 2026, or 14.1%, below the roughly 25% materiality guide. This is a sector price proxy rather than sector multiple history, so it cannot prove a stable valuation anchor; it does not trigger a cycle-elevated or cycle-depressed flag. [Web: Digrin, IGV monthly price history, accessed 2026-09-14 (unverified); iShares, IGV fund description and 2026-09-11 closing price]

## 6. Own-History Read

AKAM trades at a premium to its short own-history sample: P/LTM EPS is 28.4% above the sample mean, P/B is 14.4% above, and the vendor TEV/LTM EBITDA series is 21.3% above. This is a directional upper-range read, not evidence for a mean-reversion fair value or a valuation floor.

The biggest caveat is dual: the history is only six quarters, and the vendor EV-based series cannot be made like-for-like with the filing-based strict-EV/GAAP metrics. Falling margins, a strict-net-debt increase from $3.18bn at FY2025 to $6.08bn at Q2 FY2026, and no proven overall economic moat also weaken any presumption that an old median is warranted. [earnings/01_historical-financials, §§1, 6; business-model/99_business-model-synthesis, Verdict and pp.48–50]

The source-bound facts sidecar reports `TEV/EBITDA 13.4x vs peer set median 59.4x (high 158.2x / low 12.8x)` as the authoritative workbook read. AKAM’s 4.1% FCF yield is $629.9m filing-built LTM FCF divided by $15,345.7m market capitalization. It is not the CIQ $710.1m levered-FCF measure, which is after interest and cannot be substituted for CFO less total capex. The AKAM column contains two deliberately separate leverage bases. The 4.37x vendor number is broad: it includes operating leases in debt and nets cash plus marketable securities. The strict, filing-based number is 5.14x = $6,082.6m strict net debt / $1,184.1m GAAP-derived LTM EBITDA. They must not be substituted for one another. There is also a material AKAM reconciliation failure: the 13.4x CIQ EV/EBITDA read does not tie to the canonical filing bridge. Using $21,428.3m canonical EV and the CIQ $1,079.9m LTM EBITDA gives 19.84x, while $21,428.3m / $1,184.1m GAAP-derived EBITDA gives 18.10x. Neither equals 13.4x. This report retains 13.4x as the authoritative vendor read of that workbook, but does not use it as a valuation input. [CIQ Financials → Multiples and Income Statement, LTM June 2026; `ciq_facts.json`, `ev_ebitda_current_x` and `ltm_ebitda_m`, present; Valuation — Price & Capital Structure, §§4, 7; Earnings — Historical Financials, §2]

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| EV/EBITDA, LTM vendor basis | 13.4x | 59.4x | **(77.4%) discount** = (13.4x − 59.4x) / 59.4x |
| P/E | N/S | N/S | Not assessable |
| EV/EBIT | N/S | N/S | Not assessable |
| EV/Sales | 4.6x | N/S | Not assessable |
| FCF yield | 4.1% | N/S | Not assessable |

**Is the gap typical or unusual?** **Not assessable** — the frozen evidence has no ~3-year series of AKAM’s multiples relative to the same peer set. The vendor read also fails the filing-bridge reconciliation above, so the point-in-time 77.4% EV/EBITDA discount is not a verified relative-value signal.

## 4. Is the Gap Warranted?

**Discount is warranted, but not sizeable from the available peer matrix.** AKAM’s 5.9% LTM revenue growth trails the default-set median of 20.9%, and its 25.0% LTM EBITDA margin is below Fortinet’s 34.5%, although it is above the loss-making Cloudflare and Fastly; the broad median margin is not a meaningful quality benchmark because the group includes several loss makers. [CIQ Company Comparable Analysis, Financial Data and Operating Statistics sheets, 2026-09-14 — vendor export; Business Model — Moat, §3]

The underlying quality evidence is less favourable than a simple multiple comparison suggests: Q2 FY2026 gross margin was 55.8%, down 330 bps year on year; the business-quality score is 48/100, and the fast-changing-industry score is 35/100. The moat review finds no moat proven and reports LTM ROIC of 2.7%, while noting that its cost of capital is not assessable from the frozen evidence. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, Consolidated Statements of Income; Business Model — Business Quality, §§1–4; Business Model — Moat, §§3–5]

Finally, strict net debt/GAAP-derived EBITDA is 5.14x following May 2026 convertible issuance, a balance-sheet burden that the high-growth peers’ scattered vendor leverage fields do not measure on a matching basis. These are separate durability, growth and leverage reasons for a discount; this report does **not** apply a margin-ratio haircut to an earnings multiple. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.3–4 and Note 7, pp.17–20; Valuation — Price & Capital Structure, §5]

## 5. Implied Value from Peer Multiples

No warranted peer multiple, and therefore no peer-derived **base-case implied value**, can be defended from the frozen data. The only complete peer-multiple statistic is the heterogeneous 59.4x vendor median, and the vendor’s subject multiple fails the EV-bridge reconciliation. The calculation below is shown because it is reproducible, not because it is a fair-value estimate.

| Multiple | Applied Peer Multiple | Implied EV or Equity | Implied Price/Share | vs Current Price |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Broad default-set EV/EBITDA — mechanical only, **not a base-case value** | 59.4x LTM CIQ EBITDA | $64,146.1m EV = 59.4x × $1,079.9m; $58,063.5m equity = EV − $6,082.6m strict net debt | $377.81 = $58,063.5m / 153.686m diluted working shares | +253.8% vs $106.79 |
| Warranted peer-multiple base case | Not assessable | Not assessable | **Not assessable** | Not assessable |

The $377.81 mechanical result uses the vendor EBITDA denominator to match the vendor multiple, the canonical $6,082.6m strict net-debt bridge, and the required 153.686m diluted working share count. It is not a valid valuation range: the raw 59.4x median includes a mixture of security, cloud and software businesses with unmatched growth, profitability and capital intensity, and there is no consistent peer P/E, EV/EBIT, EV/Sales or FCF-yield dispersion from which to triangulate. [CIQ Financials → Income Statement, LTM June 2026; `ciq_facts.json`, `ltm_ebitda_m` and `peer_ev_ebitda`, present; Valuation — Price & Capital Structure, §7]

The peer-multiple dispersion is **Not assessable**. This is a partial-data outcome, not a reason to manufacture a narrower range. The closest high-value next input is a consistent, same-date Capital IQ peer export with EV, LTM/NTM revenue, EBITDA, EBIT, EPS, FCF and net debt for the named peers.

| Multiple adjusted | Peer median | Adjusted to | Gap already in the denominator? | What the extra adjustment pays for | How it was sized |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| None — no quality adjustment applied | 59.4x EV/EBITDA | N/A | Yes — EBITDA already carries the margin gap | N/A; no separate risk, durability or growth adjustment can be sized from a complete matched peer matrix | N/A |

No convergence with `02_multiples-own-history` is claimed: that method records where AKAM itself has traded and is not independent corroboration of a peer-derived value.

## 6. Sector Cycle Reality Test

**Not assessable — no sector-level multiple history.** The frozen pool has a 2026-09-14 peer snapshot but no same-basis peer-group aggregate multiple or sector-index multiple 3–5 years earlier. No cycle-elevated/depressed tag is emitted.

## 7. Relative Read

AKAM shows a 77.4% EV/EBITDA discount to Capital IQ’s broad default-set median, but the number is not a usable relative-value signal: the basket is economically mixed and the vendor’s 13.4x AKAM multiple does not reconcile to the filing-based EV bridge. AKAM’s slower growth, weaker margins versus Fortinet, declining profitability and 5.14x strict leverage support a discount, but its defensible size is not proven from the available data. The $377.81 mechanical broad-basket result is not a base-case value; a peer-based base point and cross-multiple range are **Not assessable**.
